Choosing the right undergraduate course is one of the most important decisions in a student’s life. If you are from a science background and interested in healthcare, medicine, and research, pursuing aB.Pharm coursecan be a smart and future-oriented choice.

Pharmacy is not just about dispensing medicines; it is a dynamic and rapidly growing field that connects healthcare, science, research, and patient care. A B.Pharm degree opens doors to diverse career opportunities, offering both professional stability and long-term financial growth in India and abroad.

What is B.Pharm?

The B Pharm Course (Bachelor of Pharmacy) is a four-year undergraduate degree that focuses on

Medicinal Chemistry

Pharmaceutical Analysis

Clinical Pharmacy

Drug Formulation & Development

The Bachelor ofPharmacy coursetrains students in understanding how medicines are developed, tested, manufactured, and distributed. It also provides knowledge about the safe and effective use of drugs in patient care. B Pharm Course details are vast and varied and involves learning about various chemical compounds and effect of salts on administering drugs/medicine on patients.

In India, B.Pharm is regulated by the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI), which ensures quality education and professional standards for pharmacists.

B.Pharm Eligibility Criteria

B Pharm eligibility requires 10+2 with majors in science subject like Physics, Chemistry and Biology with Mathematics.

Why Should You Choose B.Pharm?

1. Growing Pharmaceutical Industry in India

India’s pharmaceutical sector is one of the fastest-growing industries in the world. It is often referred to as the “Pharmacy of the World” because of its large-scale production and export of medicines. With increasing health awareness, chronic diseases, and demand for better healthcare services, the need for qualified pharmacists is consistently rising. This ensures job security and long-term career stability.

2. Diverse Career Options After B.Pharm

Unlike many traditional courses, B.Pharm course does not limit you to one job role. You can choose from multiple career paths based on your interests—

Clinical Practice

Pharmaceutical Research & Development

Pharmaceutical Marketing

Drug Regulatory Affairs

Government Sector Jobs

This flexibility allows you to build a career aligned with your strengths and passions.

3. Opportunity to Serve Society

Pharmacists play a crucial role in patient care. They ensure the right medicine is given at the right dose and at the right time. In hospitals and community pharmacies, pharmacists guide patients on medication usage, side effects, and drug interactions. Choosing the B.Pharm course means contributing to society by improving public health and patient safety.

4. Scope for Higher Education After B.Pharm

After completing a B.Pharm degree, you can pursue higher studies such as

M.Pharm (Master of Pharmacy)

MBA in Pharmaceutical Management

Institutes such as the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) are well-known for advanced pharmaceutical studies in India.

Higher education enhances specialisation and increases salary prospects and leadership opportunities.

5. Strong Salary and Growth Potential

The pharmaceutical industry offers competitive salary packages. Fresh graduates can start with decent entry-level salaries, and with experience and specialization, earnings increase significantly. Roles in multinational companies, research organizations, and regulatory agencies provide excellent growth opportunities.

Top 10 Future Career Opportunities After B.Pharm in India

Let’s explore the major career paths that a B.Pharm degree can provide:

1. Clinical Pharmacist

Clinical pharmacists work in hospitals and healthcare institutions. They collaborate with doctors and nurses to ensure optimal drug therapy for patients. This role requires strong knowledge of pharmacology and patient care. With the growth of multispecialty hospitals, demand for clinical pharmacists is increasing.

2. Drug Inspector

Drug inspectors ensure that pharmaceutical products meet safety and quality standards. They monitor drug manufacturing units and check compliance with regulations. This is a prestigious government job that offers stability and respect.

3. Pharmaceutical Research Scientist

If you are interested in research and innovation, you can work in Research & Development (R&D). Research scientists develop new drugs, improve existing formulations, and conduct clinical trials. Organizations like the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and pharmaceutical companies actively recruit skilled professionals in this field.

4. Quality Control and Quality Assurance Officer

Quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA) professionals ensure that medicines are manufactured according to prescribed standards. This role is critical in maintaining the safety and effectiveness of pharmaceutical products.

5. Medical Representative / Pharmaceutical Marketing

Medical representatives promote pharmaceutical products to doctors and healthcare providers. This career offers good incentives, travel opportunities, and rapid growth. With experience, you can move into managerial and marketing leadership roles.

6. Community Pharmacist

You can open your own pharmacy after registering as a licensed pharmacist. This provides an opportunity for self-employment and entrepreneurship. Running a pharmacy store can be financially stable and socially respected.

7. Regulatory Affairs Specialist

Regulatory professionals handle documentation and approvals required for launching pharmaceutical products in different countries. As global markets expand, regulatory affairs has become a high-demand and well-paid field.

8. Pharmacovigilance Officer

Pharmacovigilance involves monitoring and reporting adverse drug reactions. With strict global safety standards, this field is rapidly growing and offers opportunities in both India and abroad.

9. Government Sector Jobs

B.Pharm graduates can apply for government jobs in public health departments, railways, defence services, and regulatory authorities. Organizations like the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) offer roles related to drug regulation and safety.

10 Pharmaceutical Production Officer

The Pharmaceutical Production Officers are employed in drug manufacturing firms, and they control the production of drugs, as well as the quality and safety laws. They guarantee that products are produced in accordance with GMP and regulatory standards.

They are also likely to advance with experience into the Production Manager or Head of Plant positions, which have good earnings and career security in the pharmaceutical industry.

Stability and Long-Term Growth in B.Pharm Career

One of the biggest advantages of pursuing B.Pharm is career stability. Medicines are an essential part of healthcare, and the demand for pharmaceutical professionals does not decline easily—even during economic slowdowns. The industry continues to grow due to new diseases, technological advancements, and global healthcare demands.

With experience, pharmacists can move into managerial, research, or consultancy roles. Some even establish their own pharmaceutical manufacturing units or distribution businesses.

MLIS Course Details: Full Form, Admission, Eligibility, Duration, Fees, Colleges & Jobs

The Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) is a postgraduate professional program that aims to provide students with information, skills and abilities to handle, organize and preserve data in a variety of formats.

Both modern digital information management and traditional library methodology are covered in theMLIS course. Students enrolled in the MLIS program get an opportunity to learn how to gather, arrange, store and distribute information in both digital and physical modes efficiently.

Library science, information management (storage and retrieval), including the use of modern digital technologies, cataloging, classification, digital libraries, research methodology and knowledge management are the main topics taught in the Master's degreelibrary science program. Additionally, the course incorporates integration of IT applications, database administration and digital archiving to traditional library operations.

The MLIS master's degree bridges the gap between traditional library science and modern information technology and is suitable for students interested in managing information resources in academic, corporate, and digital environments.

Skills Required for MLIS Students

Master's of library sciences students must possess both soft and hard abilities to excel in their chosen field. Among these abilities are:

Analytical &Investigative Skills

Quantitative Skills

Ability to operate despite the stress

Interpersonal Communication Skills

MLIS full form is Master of Library and Information Science. It is a 1 year postgraduate professional degree program focused on managing, organizing, and disseminating information in both traditional libraries and digital environments, blending library science with modern technology and data skills.

Master's of Library Sciences Course and Subject Details:

The Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) course aims to develop effective information management (organizing and dissemination) skills in the students, i.e. to increase knowledge about information management within both physical and digital platforms. The course also encourages ethical and legal awareness in the use of information.

The masters of library and information science integrate:

Library Science

Information Management

Data Analytics in Libraries

Major subjects included in the MLIS curriculum are:

Cataloging and Classification

AI Applications in Libraries and Information Centres

Pharmacy Courses After 12th in India: Eligibility, Duration, Scope & Career Opportunities

The healthcare industry in India is displaying rapid growth and has emerged as a stable and lucrative career option after the 12th standard. Pharmacy courses after 12 in India combine healthcare skills with their scientific expertise.

Below is a detailed overview ofpharmacy courses after 12th in India, detailing eligibility criteria, popular course options, course duration, fees, career scope & opportunities for jobs.

Pharmacy Courses After 12th in India:

The pharmacy course covers the know-how of medicines such as their preparation, dispensing methods and their appropriate usage. The course is suitable for students with an interest in medicine, chemistry and healthcare.

The Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) are the regulatory bodies that govern pharmacy courses in India. After completing 12th standard, students can opt for a diploma, undergraduate, or integrated pharmacy course based on their career goals and academic background.

Popular Pharmacy Courses After 12th Include:

Diploma in Pharmacy (D. Pharma)

Bachelor of Pharmacy (B. Pharma)

In today’s prevalence of wild mash-up of tech gadgets, money and biotech wizardry, we are forgetting agriculture, which has been holding us, humans up since forever and is literally the spine of civilizations. With increasing challenges such as climate change, food security, sustainable farming, shortage of fertile land, and ever increasing population, advanced research and innovation in agriculture are now more badly needed than ever.

Pursuing aPhD in Agriculture courseis now a highly valuable academic and professional choice for students who aspire to contribute to this vital aspect and land a career that actually matters.

Understanding the PhD Agriculture Program:

A PhD in Agriculture Program is the highest academic qualification in agricultural sciences. The course is highly academic research intensive and deals with developing advanced expertise, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills. The course is completed in 3 to 6 years, depending on the nature of research, mode of study ie. full-time PhD in Agriculture or part-time PhD in Agriculture and constrained by institutional guidelines.

The course curriculum focuses on research, publication of scholarly papers and submission of a thesis. Students are under the guidance of experienced supervisors and contribute to finding solutions for real-world agricultural problems. An example could be researching drought-resistant rice, testing in muddy fields, and solving problems farmers actually face. The course is suitable for candidates who are into research, teaching, policy decisions or other roles in agriculture and associated sectors.

PhD Agriculture Admission: Eligibility and Selection:

Students holding a postgraduate degree (MSc/ MTech) in Agriculture or a related discipline with a minimum percentage as specified by the university are eligible for PhD Agriculture Admission. Students are considered for the course based on national-level entrance examinations ie ICAR-NET, CSIR-NET or university-specific entrance tests, followed by an interview.

The admission process evaluates past academic performance, research aptitude, agriculture knowledge and prior research papers, if any. Getting admitted in a reputed institution significantly fuels career prospects.

Research in these unique areas plays a crucial role.

Full-Time PhD in Agriculture vs Part-Time PhD in Agriculture:

For working professionals, a part-time PhD in Agriculture lets them juggle academic and professional commitment thereby providing a unique opportunity for future growth without the need for career breaks.

There are several prestigious career paths after completing a PhD in Agriculture beyond teaching. After completing standard 12th, it is one such important juncture of life where students need to take the right decision to pursue their career in the desired direction. This blog will give you an insight on a career in Law after 12th in India. Lawyers in India is a respectable career choice for students who want to pursue a career in the field of Law, legal studies, governance, justice, corporate law, company law, and legal practice etc. There are many integrated law programmes after 12th available in various Indian colleges and universities where the courses are approved by the Bar Council of India (BCI) that ensures a structured legal education and professional pathway for the future.

This complete step-by-step guide explains eligibility for law after 12th, law entrance exams in India,law courses, skills required to become a lawyer, career options in law, and future prospects for aspiring lawyers in India.

Step 1: Complete Class 12 from a Recognized Board

The aspirant of law should have completed standard 10+2 from a recognized board such as State Board, ICSE, or CBSE from any stream—Arts, Science, or Commerce are eligible to apply for law programmes after 12th with a minimum aggregate requirement of 45% marks.

Step 2: Choose the Right Law Course After 12th

After Class 12, students must enroll in a 5-year Integrated Law Degree, which combines an undergraduate degree with a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.).

Popular integrated law courses after 12th in India include:

BA LL.B. (Arts + Law)

BBA LL.B. (Management + Law)

BCom LL.B. (Commerce + Law)

BSc LL.B. (Science + Law)

These BCI-approved law courses are offered by National Law Universities (NLUs), private law colleges, and government law colleges in India.

Read Also-How to Choose the Right Law Program After 12th: A Beginner's Guide

Step 3: Appear for Law Entrance Exams

Admission to reputed law colleges in India after 12th is primarily through entrance examinations. Major law entrance exams in India include:

CLAT (Common Law Admission Test): For admission to NLUs across India

AILET exam: Conducted by National Law University, Delhi

SLAT exam: For Symbiosis Law Schools

LSAT–India exam: Accepted by several private universities

University-level law entrance exams: Conducted by individual institutions

Preparation usually starts in Class 11 or Class 12 and focuses on subjects such as English, Logical Reasoning, Legal Aptitude, General Knowledge, Current Affairs, and Quantitative Techniques.

Step 4: Complete the 5-Year Integrated Law Degree

The 5-year integrated law course typically spans 10 semesters and includes both academic and practical legal training. Core subjects studied during the course include:

Constitutional Law

Criminal Law (IPC, CrPC)

Along with classroom learning, students must complete mandatory law internships with advocates, law firms, courts, NGOs, and corporate legal departments to gain practical exposure in legal practice.

Step 5: Develop Essential Skills During Law School

To succeed as a lawyer, students must develop essential skills required to become a lawyer alongside academic learning. These include:

Strong communication and advocacy skills

Legal research and drafting

Analytical and critical thinking

Negotiation and client-handling skills

Time management and ethical judgment

Participating in moot court competitions, debates, legal aid clinics, and law internships greatly enhances practical competence.

Step 6: Enroll with the State Bar Council

After completing theLL.B. degree, it is mandatory for graduates to enroll with the State Bar Council to practice law legally and to be recognized as a lawyer in India.

Read Also-BA LLB Course Details: Full Form, Admission, Eligibility, Duration, Fees, Colleges, Jobs

Step 7: Clear the All India Bar Examination (AIBE)

The All India Bar Examination (AIBE) is conducted by the Bar Council of India. Clearing this exam is compulsory to obtain the Certificate of Practice, which legally authorizes a candidate to practice as an advocate in Indian courts.

The AIBE tests basic legal knowledge and is qualifying in nature, not ranking-based.

Step 8: Start Legal Practice or Choose a Career Path

Once licensed, lawyers can choose from diverse career options after law in India such as:

Litigation Lawyer: Practice in District Courts, High Courts, or the Supreme Court

Corporate Lawyer: Work with law firms or corporate legal teams

Judicial Services: Prepare for judiciary exams to become a judge

Legal Advisor: Work with companies, NGOs, or government bodies

Academics: Pursue LL.M. and become a law professor or researcher

Civil Services & Public Policy: Law graduates have an advantage in UPSC and state services

Step 9: Higher Studies and Specialization (Optional)

After LL.B., students may pursueLL.M. after law to specialize in areas like Constitutional Law, Corporate Law, Criminal Law, International Law, and Intellectual Property Rights (IPR). Further options include Ph.D. in Law or diploma certifications.

Step 10: Career Growth and Long-Term Prospects

Law is a profession where experience in legal practice matters. Initial years may be challenging, especially in litigation, but with persistence, reputation, and specialization, lawyers can achieve career growth in law, financial stability, and social respect.

BA and BBA are three-year undergraduate degrees that offer different career progressions having fundamentally different objectives after Class 12.BA coursefocuses on humanities and social sciences. On the other side BBA stresses on business, management and corporate careers.

BA vs BBA: Subject Focus

BA (Bachelor of Arts) deals with humanities and social sciences like Economics, English, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, etc.BBA coursedeals with business management subjects such as marketing, finance, human resources, operations and entrepreneurship with a more practical and industry-oriented approach. Both degrees are 3-year Undergraduate programs and if pursued from recognized universities can be used as a foundation for higher studies like MA, MBA and professional or competitive exams.

Eligibility Criteria for BA and BBA

Eligibility criteria for both streams are typically similar, and BA and BBA accepts students from any stream (Arts/ Commerce/ Science) who have passed Class 12 from a recognized board with 45-50% marks. Some institutions can conduct entrance tests and interview for BBA aspirants. While deciding between the two, preference and knack for particular course as well as future roles can be a consideration.

BA Course Structure and Teaching Methodology

Bachelor ofArts coursefocuses on subjects in humanities/ social sciences with flexibility to choose majors and electives such as Economics, English, History, Political Science, Psychology or Sociology. The teaching methodology for BA courses is conceptual and theoretical, leading to critical thinking, reading, writing and research skills rather than hands-on corporate exposure.

BBA Programs Structure and Teaching Methodology

While BBA programs focus on business subjects such as Fundamentals, Marketing, Finance, Business Economics, HR, Business Law, Business Analytics and Operations. In the BBA course, the teaching methodology is practical, with case studies, projects, internships, presentations and simulations to prepare students for corporate roles from the undergraduate level itself. Choosing BBA is ideal for aspirants looking to advance their careers in management or strategic responsibilities or aspire for leadership roles making them versatile professionals. The BBA program develops data analysis, critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities..

Aspirant may go for BA if he/ she has strong interest in humanities, languages, social sciences or public policy and enjoy reading, writing and theoretical subjects and considering careers in academics, civil services, media, social sector or planning to pursue specialized postgraduate degrees like MA, MSW, Journalism or competitive exams.

Aspirants can choose BBA if he/ she is inclined toward business, management, startups, corporate jobs and like applied, practical learning with internships and projects and considering career in entry corporate roles (marketing, HR, finance, operations, business development) or planning to pursue an MBA later for higher managerial or leadership positions.

Aspirants choice can be guided by their preference, the desired career and whether they visualize seeing themselves analyzing society and ideas or managing teams, brands and businesses.

GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is a highly competitive Indian national level examination that measures all-round knowledge in the fields of engineering, technology, science, architecture and humanity and is a prerequisite in Master/Doctoral admissions to the best institutes (IISc/IITs) as well as recruitment in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).

Why is GATE Important?

TheGraduate Aptitude Test in Engineering(GATE) is a national-level examination, conducted jointly by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and seven Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) to adjudge students comprehension of knowledge in engineering, technology, architecture, science, and humanities. GATE serves as a qualifying examination for admission in higher education and also for employment in professional careers by several organizations mostly Public Sectors.

Every year, several students and working professionals appear for the GATE exam to secure admission into master's programs in engineering, doctoral programs in engineering, and institutions such as IITs, NITs, IIITs, IISc, and other top research universities. Qualifying GATE enables students to apply for Junior Research Fellowships (JRF), pursue research roles in ISRO/ DRDO labs, and receive stipends through MHRD scholarships during postgraduate studies. GATE scores are also used for admission to master's and doctoral programs at some foreign universities, such as in Singapore and Germany.

Beyond higher education qualifying examination, GATE scores are also widely used by various Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)—including BHEL, ONGC, NTPC, IOCL, and HPCL for job opportunities at executive level. GATE tests understanding of conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Its specialization options now include interdisciplinary subjects, offering opportunities to a wider class of students.

Eligibility Criteria for GATE Exam after 12th

Educational Qualification & Eligible Degrees

To be eligible for GATE examination, authorities have widened the variety of eligible disciplines beyond just engineering and technology. Candidates must be Holding (or currently enrolled in) an undergraduate degree in Engineering / Technology / Architecture / Pharmacy / Science / Commerce / Arts / Humanities from a recognized institute (eg. B.E. / B.Tech / B.Arch / B.Pharm/ B.Sc (Research) / B.S / Post-Diploma-based B.Sc programs);

Or holding (or enrolled in) a postgraduate degree (e.g. M.Sc / M.A / MCA) in a relevant subject (for certain GATE papers);

Or enrolled in / have completed integrated or dual-degree programs (e.g. integrated B.Tech + M.Tech, or similar (including professional-society-certified degrees recognized by MoE/ AICTE/ UPSC).

Final and Pre-Final year students can also write GATE examination which provides flexibility to appear in GATE early and potentially secure admission or plan for future higher studies even before graduation.

Number of Attempts

Subject to fulfillment of other requirements, GATE allows unlimited attempts and there is no limit on how many times you can write GATE examination. This unlimited-attempt policy gives a better chance to improve performance and get better ranks or keep options open for higher studies or PSU recruitment.

Year of Qualification

Students must ensure that they are in the eligible year required to take GATE examination ie, typically 3rd year or above for bachelor’s degrees, or final year.

Documents Required During Application

GATE application requires scanned copies of following documents in prescribed formats (e.g., JPG/JPEG for photo/ signature at 20-200 KB and PDF for certificates):

Photograph: Recent color photo (face covering 60-70% of frame), JPG/JPEG, 20-200;

Clear scanned image on white background of signature (JPG/ JPEG, 5-200 KB);

Scanned copy of valid Photo ID such as Aadhaar (preferred), Passport, PAN Card, Voter ID, or Driving License in which the name and DOB of the applicant matches. These are required to be carried in original to exam center;

Category Certificate (SC/ ST/ OBC-NCL/ EWS, as applicable) issued by competent authority in PDF format;

PwD/ UDID Certificate (as applicable) in PDF fromat issued by authorized medical authority;

Dyslexia Certificate (as applicable) in PDF format.?

While submitting the application, personal details like name (matching with the Photo ID), DOB, mobile/ email, address, eligibility degree information shall be required. Foreign candidates require Passport as Photo ID proof. Students are advised to visit official GATE 2026 site for exact details if any update.?

International Students

GATE isn’t restricted to Indian nationals alone. International candidates (from recognized countries) are eligible if they meet the educational requirements.

Key Features of GATE Examination

Second Chances & Lifelong Learning

Since there’s no limit on number of attempts or on age, it provides students chances to crack in several chances even after few years, change in career path, or additional education. The format of the examination also permits improvement of the score.

Freedom for Non-Engineering Backgrounds

Students from science, arts, commerce — or those with three-year degrees are also eligible for GATE examination to secure admissions in higher studies in technical/ interdisciplinary courses.

Work + Study Friendly

Working professionals who took a break, or who want to study alongside work, can appear for GATE and is very useful for mid-career ambitions or research aspirations.

Equal Opportunity

Whether you're a fresh graduate or an experienced engineer, you get the equal chances for appearing and scoring in the examinations.

The JEE Main entrance exam is one of the toughest undergraduate engineering entrance tests worldwide, with thousands of students competing for limited seats. Cracking JEE Main on the first attempt, even though daunting, can be achieved with the right planning, steady effort, and smart strategy.

Know Your Exam inside out:

Before jumping into preparation mode, it's important to strategize by understanding the structure of theJEE Mainsexamination. The exam tests three core subjects: Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Questions are objective — including single correct options and numerical-based problems. While attempting the examination, what matters most is clarity of concepts, speed of solving problems, and accuracy under defined timelines.

Clarity over Exam Pattern

Knowing the exam pattern and syllabus right from the start gives you a more effective preparation strategy — rather than just random studying. For example, there are usually around 75 questions total—25 from each subject—split between multiple-choice and numerical value questions you have to solve precisely. Getting comfortable with this format early on saves you from surprises later.

Read Also-Top 10 Engineering Colleges Offering Admission Without JEE Mains

Start with a Realistic, Well-Structured Study Plan:

The preparation of achievable study plan is the primary stepping stone for successful preparation for acing JEE Main. We would suggest breaking down entire syllabus of each subject in smaller portions/ key concepts and allocate specific time for such portion of each subject. For example, devote 6 to 8 hours daily to focused study. Students must focus on tough topics upfront rather than pushing them off until later.

Revision is the Key

Keep some time in weekend for revising and consolidating the progress throughout the week. Consistency matters more than intense but irregular study sprints. Disciplined schedule with small, achievable goals helps maintain momentum and avoids burnout. If you’re also attempting board exams alongside preparation forJoint Entrance Exam mainssplitting study time between board syllabus (especially overlapping chapters) and JEE mains preparation shall be required.

Master the Basics Fundamentals and choose right study materials:

Many students does mistake in going for advanced books too early and confusing the conepts. We would suggest to initially stick with NCERT textbooks for Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics for building core fundamental concepts. It might be worthwhile to add that many of JEE questions are prepared from NCERT text book concepts. Once you have completed NCERT text book and are confident, students can move to other advanced reference books like H. C. Verma for Physics, D. Sharma for Maths, and P. Tandon for Chemistry. Students can also access videos available on different platforms for fresh oversight on the concepts and to deepen their understanding. Students can also use exams practice platforms for large numbers of practice problems to keep your skills sharp.

Read Also-List of Best Engineering Colleges after 12th in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh

Understand the concepts, Don’t Just Memorize:

JEE exams does not test memory skills of the students but rather “why” and “how” behind formulas and theories. Students must instead focus on really understanding the “why” and “how” behind everything. For instance, in Physics, don’t just memorize equations—understand their derivations, key assumptions and how they apply to real scenarios. In Math, practice variety of problems to develop alternate thinking skills. Chemistry is easier when you grasp reaction mechanisms instead of just memorizing reaction lists.

Practice Makes Perfect- Mock Tests, Previous-Year Papers & Problem Solving:

After learning fundamental concepts practice becomes necessary to ace the JEE main exams. Aspirants must past years JEE question papers, full length mock exams to get a feel for the real thing. Take mock tests regularly eg 2 to 3 a week and analyze the questions where you went wrong which will help you build upon the conceptual understanding. While taking these tests, simulate real world limitations like the actual exam with no distractions under time limit. This builds your speed and confidence (and beats exam anxiety too).

Manage Time Smartly:

Time management is critical both during your preparation and on exam day and requires discipline. During preparation, divide your time among subjects, spending extra time on weaker areas. Don’t overwhelm your time schedule and take small breaks to stay fresh.

On exam day, start with your strengths or easiest questions to get dose of momentum and confidence. Don’t get stuck on any question and move on keeping it for later when coming back as and when time allows. Focus on accuracy for sure marks rather than chasing every tough question.

Don’t Neglect Revision:

Revision is critical tool for preparation and students must revisit topics multiple times through mock tests to deep dive in fundamentals and reduce mistakes. Keep handy short notes or formula sheets for quick revision during the last stretch just before the exam.

Take Care of Yourself physically and mentally:

Physical and mental stress and fatigue are as critical as the preparation students have done. Long hours of study lose their effectiveness if your brain is fatigued or stressed. Students are advised to get 6-7 hours of sleep every night, eat nutritious meals, and stay hydrated. Students must also be fit physically can go for short walks or meditation.

Avoid common mistakes& Stay Consistent:

Many students could not crack JEE on the first shot because of simple mistakes, like jumping straight to advanced books without basics, ignoring revision, mock tests, right strategy. Students must plan to study steadily, practice smartly and revise regularly.

Read Also-Top Reasons Why You Choose Mangalayatan University Aligarh for a Successful Career

Keep Your Spirits High:

JEE mains preparation can be stressful for students, so keep your motivation alive. Set small achievable targets, like finishing a chapter or acing a mock test, and reward yourself when you achieve them. Socialize with similar aspirants who are encouraging or mentors. Stay calm on exam day and proceed to solve questions on your strength topics and if a question is tough—flag and move on.

Choosing between an MBA and a PGDM is a common issue for management students as both courses are related to developing business knowledge, inculcating leadership skills, and making students ready for jobs. The difference between the two lies in the structure, curriculum, approving agencies and approach of delivering the outcome. Students need to understand these subtle differences to analyze and choose the best career decision aligned with their goals, interests, and future plans.

Understanding MBA and PGDM

An MBA (Master of Business Administration) is a degree program offered by universities or colleges affiliated with universities. The approving and regulatory agency for the MBA course is the University Grants Commission (UGC).

PGDM (Post Graduate Diploma in Management) is a diploma course offered by autonomous colleges. The approving and regulatory agency for the PGDM course is the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). Many top management institutes like IIMs, XLRI, SPJIMR, MDI etc offer PGDM programs.

Though completion of theMBA courseleads to degree while the PGDM course leads to a diploma, they both hold similar recognition and value in the industry, depending upon the reputation of the institution.

Key Differences Between MBA and PGDM Program

Curriculum Structure:

MBA courses are more oriented towards theory and designed & imparted by Universities. The course may be outdated and less dynamic in a few cases, as any change in the curriculum requires regulatory approvals.

At the same timePGDBM coursesare designed to be flexible, practical, agile and based on real-life industry situations. Being imparted by autonomous colleges, the course content is more agile and can be adapted quickly to fast changes in market, technology and industry requirements.

PGDM course scores over this point being quickly adaptable and relevant for modern business roles.Winner - PGDMin terms of curriculum relevance.

Teaching Style & Learning Experience:

The MBA course being more oriented towards theory the course content delivery tends to be more academic stressing on theoretical management concepts.

While PGDM course being more industry oriented, the course content delivery focuses on practical teaching including case studies, group projects, live simulations, real life industry projects, field work, internships, and corporate interactions.

Winner - PGDMin terms of industry exposure while learning.

Program Regulation:

The MBA course is regulated and approved by University Grants Commission (UGC).

At the same time, the PGDM course is regulated and approved by All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE).

Both are recognized and holds equal value, but the regulatory agency are different. The regulatory bodies only influence the curriculum freedom to the institutes but are equal in terms recognition and value in industry.Winner - Both MBA and PGDM courses hold equal value and recognition.

Value in India and Abroad:

In India, both MBA and PGDM courses holds equal value and recognition and are widely accepted. Employers focus more on reputation of the institute reputation, the skills acquired by the students and performance records rather than whether the qualification is a degree or diploma.

While in abroad, an MBA degree is frequently more recognized for higher education ie, PhD admissions by foreign universities. Some PGDM programs may require conversion to an MBA or equivalent before being recognized in abroad.Winner - MBAfor higher studies abroad.

MBA vs PGDM Course Duration:

Both MBA and PGDM courses are generally 2-year courses however, some institutes may offer executive or accelerated 1-year course for working professionals.Winner - BothMBA and PGDM are usually of same duration.

MBA vs PGDM Admission Fee Structure:

The MBA courses being offered by universities or colleges affiliated from universities are lower in cost and affordable as universities receive government support in various funding. The course fees are very nominal in MBA programs in government colleges and public universities thereby having better ROI.

While the PGDM courses are more expensive due to greater autonomy, cost of industry collaborations and infrastructure cost. Premier institutes offering PGDM courses charge significantly higher fees based upon their recognition in employability.Winner - MBAin terms of cost and affordability.

Industry Acceptance & Job Opportunities:

After completion of both MBA and PGDM courses, students get equally excellent job opportunities. However, the job profile and outcomes depend heavily on various factors such as:

Institution Reputation;

Specialization;

Industry relevant skills acquired by the student during the course; and

Industry trends

Industries does not distinguish much between MBA and PGDM courses while employing however, based on institute reputation, PGDM from a top institute shall outperform an MBA from an average college.Winner - PGDMscores higher based on the institute reputation.

Specialization Options:

Both MBA and PGDM usually offer similar specializations eg, Marketing, Finance, Human Resource Management, Operations, Business Analytics, International Business, Supply Chain Management.

However, PGDM institutes being more flexible and agile are able to introduce new specialization to meet rapidly changing requirements in the industries, may offer new-age specializations eg, Digital Marketing, AI & Data Science, Financial Technology, Product Management, Entrepreneurship & InnovationWinner - PGDMdue to wider specialization offering including modern and trending specializations.

Read Also-PGDM Course Details: Full Form, Admission, Eligibility, Entrance Exam, Fees, and Colleges

Placement Support:

Universities offering MBA courses with strong alumni networks and industry relationships provide good placements, but the results varies widely among different colleges/ universities.

At the same time, autonomous institutes offering PGDM courses outperform placement results of MBA especially by reputable institutes. The top-tier institutes often have better placement performance, stronger corporate ties and structured internship programs due to industry collaboration.Winner - PGDM, especially from well-established and reputed institutes.

Which One Should You Choose?

In reference to above discussions, students can easily understand that there is no absolute winner between the two MBA and PGDM. Students must weigh each consideration based upon their desired career goals, budget, learning outcome expectation and future plans.

Students may choose MBA if:

Prefer a degree program with wider recognized academic status including abroad;

Based on future plans for higher studies, pursuing PhD or academic research in India or abroad;

Affordability considering the expenditure required for completing the course;

Prefer theory-based learning approach;

Preference for public universities or government institutions with strong reputations.

Students may choose PGDM if:

Prefer more relevant, industry trend aligned courses with real life scenarios;

Prefer a agile and dynamic curriculum aligned with the latest industry requirements;

Aiming for versatile roles in corporate leadership, consulting, analytics, or entrepreneurship;

Afford courses from top PGDM institutes like IIMs, XLRI, MDI, or private institution with excellent placement records;

Require exposure to real life case studies, industry readiness by internships, corporate tie-ups.

Enhance Your Career Growth with aMBA vs PGDM Program

MBA vs PGDM Program

MBA vs PGDM: Which is Better Overall?

In India, both MBA and PGDM are equally recognized and employable qualifications. Rather than the degree or diploma, what matters is the reputation and quality of the institute and their faculty, placement records and industry exposure. To summarize,

PGDM from a top institution provides more value than an MBA from an average college. At the same time, MBA from a reputed university is better than a PGDM from a lesser-known private institution.

Hence, instead of asking “Which is better: MBA vs PGDM?”, focus should rather be on "Which college or institute will provide me the strongest platform for my career?

Future opportunities shall depend on the choices of institution, efforts during the course, selected specialization and effective application of the learning.

Specialisation in M. Pharm. Course

Following typical specialization are offered in M. Pharm. course:

Pharmaceutics- The specialization deals with Drug Delivery Systems; Molecular Pharmaceutics;; Advanced Biopharmaceutics & Pharmacokinetics, Cosmetics and Cosmeceuticals.

Industrial Pharmacy- The specialization deals with Advanced Industrial Pharmacy; Pharmaceutical Production and Process Technology, Regulatory interfaces for manufacturing.

Pharmaceutical Chemistry- The specialisation deals with advanced organic and medicinal chemistry, spectroscopic and Computer-Aided Drug Design, and Process Chemistry.

Pharmaceutical Analysis- The specialization deals with Advanced Instrumental Analysis, Modern Bio-Analytical Techniques, Quality Control & Quality Assurance, Herbal/Cosmetic Analysis.

Quality Assurance- The specialization deals with Quality Systems and GMP, Validation and Qualification, Regulatory Compliance and Audits.

Regulatory Affairs- The specialization deals with Drug, Device, and Dossier Requirements; Global submissions, Food & Nutraceuticals regulations.

Pharmaceutical Biotechnology- The specialization deals with Bioprocess Engineering, Biopharmaceuticals and Fermentation Technology, Genetic Engineering applications.

Pharmacy Practice- The specialization deals with Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, Pharma covigilance, Hospital and Community Pharmacy practice.

Pharmacology- The specialization deals with Advanced Pharmacology and Toxicology, Preclinical screening and Evaluation Methods, Pharmacokinetics.

Pharmacognosy- The specialization deals with Phytochemistry and Natural Products, Herbal Drug Technology, Nutraceuticals and marine/ novel sources.

M. Pharm. Course Fees

The Course fees for M. Pharm. is typically Rs. 90,000/- per year I.e. a total tuition fees of Rs. 1,80,000/- for entire 2 year duration with a small amount for registration charges, examination fees and security deposit etc.

What is an Online MBA for Working Professionals in India?

An online MBA for working professionals is a flexible, typically 2 years, postgraduate degree program delivered virtually, allowing individuals to gain management expertise without halting their careers.

Definition and Overview

An online MBA enables students to secure a business degree without straining their other commitments in life. In an Online MBA program, students study the same topics as a regular on campus MBA program such as — finance, marketing, HR, operations which can be studied from anywhere.

In an Online MBA program, students gets a combination of live virtual sessions, recorded lectures, and interactive discussions. Students are also engaged in projects, work across team, networking across industries and geographic zones.

Why Students Choose Online MBA for Working Professionals Program in India

The accredited Online MBA program are designed for working professionals letting them study while balancing work, home commitments with smart time management and, if available, employer support. For working professionals, combining the theory and practical learning of Online MBA program with work experience turns the program into an skill building investment leading to long-term career growth.

Difference Between Online MBA and Distance MBA:

An Online MBA program involves a live, digital classroom where students join video classes, discuss and get feedback with plenty of interactive content. While a Distance MBA program is a Do It Yourself course where you get the course material or pre-recorded lectures, study on their own and take exams at a test centre.

An online MBA program should be preferred which provides higher interaction and flexibility of learning from anywhere. Distance MBA program can be opted for in case the student is comfortable to study on their own with no requirement for live classes and self-paced study.

Benefits of Pursuing an Online MBA

Flexibility for Working Professionals:

An online MBA offers flexibility to study around work and family, without pausing your career. Balancing work, home, and academics can be challenging, but it’s achievable with smart time management and, if available, employer support. Many organizations encourage further education through sponsoring, better job profiles, and higher remuneration.

Career Advancement and Global Exposure:

Career growth happens by acquiring new skills, sharpening leadership acumen and act strategically. Students gets return of their hard work by promotions, salary hike and advancing the career into strategic roles.

Brainstorming with classmates crossing geographical boundaries widens your perspective and gets you access to great faculty and tackling real cross-border cases.

Networking Opportunities in Online Learning:

Online learning makes it convenient to meet people across geographical boundaries. Use of online tools such as video discussions, webinars, live Q&As makes trading ideas, building camaraderie, learning from other experienced members quite easy thereby opening doors to a global network broadening perspective and moving career forward.

BLIS Course Details: Full Form. Admission, Eligibility, Duration, Fees, Colleges, Jobs

The Bachelor of Library and Information Science (BLIS) - A one-year undergraduate professional degree program called the Bachelor of Library and Information Science (BLIS) prepares students for jobs in knowledge organization, information handling, and library management. The course gives students the tools they need to effectively gather, organize, catalog, and handle a variety of information resources, both digital and analog. Students have hands-on experience with information retrieval methods, library software, and contemporary digital technologies that provide online information services and e-libraries.

Graduates of theBLIS degreemight find employment in corporate information centers, archives, public libraries, university libraries, and the field of digital knowledge management thanks to its emphasis on research technique, communication skills, and user-centered services. For those who have a strong interest in literature, knowledge systems, and information technology, this curriculum is perfect because it gives them access to chances in both government.

BLIS stands for Bachelor of Library and Information Science. It is a professional one year undergraduate degree program that emphasizes on how to manage libraries, organize information, and handle digital resources. The future of BLIS seems bright given the increasing significance of knowledge management and the move to digital libraries.

Graduates can work at educational institutions, research organizations, government agencies, corporations, digital platforms, and as librarians, information officers, archivists, documentation specialists, and knowledge managers. Because of the increased opportunities brought about by the growth of e-libraries, online databases, and digital information systems, BLIS experts are crucial to the efficient management, preservation, and distribution of information. BLIS graduates can also pursue research-focused programs or further degrees like MLIS (Master of Library and Information Science), which will further their academic and professional development.

BLIS Course Details

A BLIS course is a Bachelor of Library and Information Sciences which is a bachelors degree that provides knowledge on the basics of administration and arrangement of libraries, information centers, and archives. The one-year program majorly concentrates on the cataloging, classification, management of resources and information services and graduate students are prepared to work as librarians, library assistants and archivists.

Eligibility Criteria for Bachelor of Library and Information Science (BLIS)

Candidate should have completed a Bachelor’s degree (in any discipline) from a recognized university.

For admission in BLIS course, the minimum required marks is 45%.

Students from any stream – Arts, Science, or Commerce – are eligible.

There is no specific age limit; both fresh graduates and working professionals can apply.

Admission is generally merit-based (marks in graduation), though some institutions may conduct entrance tests or interviews.

Career Prospects after pursuing Bachelor of Library and Information Science

Librarian:Manage resources and services at public libraries, colleges, institutions, and schools.

Information Officer/Specialist:Manage databases, digital content, and information systems in government and business institutions.

Archivist:Maintain historical records, manuscripts, and digital archives in research institutions, museums, and archives.

Documentation Officer:Oversee research publications, reports, and technical documentation in companies and R&D facilities.

Digital Librarian/E-Librarian:Utilize contemporary software technologies to manage digital libraries, e-books, and online resources.

Corporate Knowledge Manager:Organize and oversee knowledge systems in enterprises and global corporations.

Teaching and Research:Pursue advanced degrees such as MLIS, M.Phil., or Ph.D. for positions in academia and research.

Government Jobs:Opportunities at public service commissions, universities, government libraries, and ministries.

Global Scope:Work in universities, international organizations, and digital information centers overseas.

Entrepreneurship:Startups in digital information consultancy, library setup services, or knowledge management firms.

MBA and M.Tech courses offer different career progressions having fundamentally different objectives. MBA stresses on business management, leadership, strategy, finance to prepare graduates for managerial and C-suite roles in variety of industries, such as consulting, HR, marketing and finance. On the other side, the M.Tech course prepares graduates for specialization in technical and development roles by enhancing their technical and engineering expertise in specific areas such as core engineering discipline eg. electrical, mechanical systems, Information systems, emerging technologies such as AI.

Eligibility criteria for both streams differs, whileMBA courseaccepts graduates from any field on the other hand M.Tech requires a graduate in core engineering branches background. Similarly, the career pathways vary while MBA graduates can expect them to be in managerial or strategic roles, whereas M. Tech graduates can be absorbed in technical roles requiring deep insight into the specific domain areas.?

While deciding between the two, preference and knack for particular course as well as future roles can be a consideration. MTech provides advanced technical expertise and opportunities in R&D, product development, or academia. M.Tech can be chosen to further engineering knowledge and looking for careers in academics, technical innovation, or research. While MBA can be pursued if the student wishes to go for management or strategic responsibilities, or aspire for leadership roles. Choosing an MBA is ideal for individuals aiming to advance their careers in management making them versatile professionals. The MBA program develops data analysis, critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities.

A Master inBusiness Administration Courseis a two-year postgraduate qualification designed to equip students with advanced business skills and comprehensive knowledge, data analysis, critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving abilities.

In the case of specializations in MBA courses, students can deep dive into certain core areas such as finance, marketing, HR or healthcare management. The specialization in a MBA program offer students opportunity to align their skill set with their career aspirations thereby increasing their expertise and industry readiness in their chosen field. M.Tech. Admission

To be eligible forM.Tech admissionstudents must be holding a engineering graduation degree in relevant field with at least 50% of the required marks. These standards guarantee that students possess the skills and background required for further study in the engineering field of their choice.

The University offers M.Tech. in different specialization in all core branches I.e. Computer Science Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering. The duration of an M.Tech (Master of Technology) in Engineering is 2 years which is divided into 4 semesters.

M.Tech Course Details

The M.Tech in Computer Science Engineering (CSE) typically covers specialization in advanced computing concepts, algorithms, data structures, machine learning, artificial intelligence, cyber security, cloud computing, big data analytics, and software development. Students may specialize in areas like AI, data science, or networking.

The M.Tech in Civil Engineering (CE) typically covers specialization in structural engineering, geotechnical engineering, transportation engineering, construction management, environmental engineering, water resources, and sustainable infrastructure.

The M.Tech in Mechanical Engineering (ME) typically covers specialization in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, manufacturing processes, CAD/CAM, materials science, and energy systems. Students upgrade their skill set in designing, production, and maintenance of mechanical systems.

The M.Tech in Electrical Engineering (EE) typically covers specialization in power systems, control systems, electrical machines, renewable energy, high-voltage engineering. Students upgrade their skill set in designing, operating, maintaining, and optimizing electrical systems.

The M.Tech in Electronics Engineering (EnC) typically covers specialization in VLSI design, embedded systems, communication systems, signal processing, microelectronics, and instrumentation. Students upgrade their skill set in designing and developing electronic devices and communication technologies. MJMC Course Details: Full Form. Admission, Eligibility, Duration, Fees, Colleges, Jobs

A Master of Journalism and Mass Communication (MJMC) is a postgraduate degree developed for individuals who want to pursue a successful career in media, communication, or allied sectors. This study typically lasts two years and focuses on both academic understanding and practical skills required in today's rapidly changing media industry. Students study news reporting, media ethics, public relations, advertising, digital journalism, and broadcast media.

One of the most notable aspects of a MJMC curriculum is the emphasis on critical thinking, research, and communication skills. With the rise of digital platforms, the course now teaches students multimodal storytelling, content creation, and the use of current communication technologies. Workshops, internships, and live projects all provide additional real-world experience and increase employability.

After finishing theMJMC course, there are numerous and diverse career choices available. Graduates can pursue careers as journalists, editors, news anchors, public relations officers, content writers, media planners, advertising experts, or communication specialists in both public and commercial sectors. In addition, they can pursue academic or research positions in media studies.

Overall, a MJMC program is great for students who are passionate about media and communication, as it provides a platform for them to influence public opinion, successfully communicate knowledge, and make meaningful contributions to society.

MJMC stands for Master of Journalism and Mass Communication. It is a 2-year postgraduate degree program that fosters advanced learning in Mass Media, print media, public relation, digital communication, and journalism.

MJMC Course Details

MJMC is a two-year postgraduate program that focuses on advanced knowledge and skills in media, journalism, and communications. The course is aimed at graduates who desire to work in print, broadcast, or digital media, as well as advertising, public relations, and corporate communication.

The MJMCJournalism and Mass Communication coursecurriculum covers a wide range of topics, including media law and ethics, reporting and editing, development communication, new media technologies, advertising techniques, and public relations management. With the expanding importance of digital platforms, students are also taught multimedia content development, social media management, and online journalism. Along with classroom instruction, the course emphasizes practical training through internships, workshops, field visits, and live projects, allowing students to gain industry experience.

Pharm D Course Details: Full Form, Eligibility, Fees, Admission, Top Colleges and Scope

The Pharm.D (Doctor of Pharmacy)? programme at Mangalayatan University has a course duration of six years, and in return, students earn a doctorate in Pharmacy. The program is designed to educate students about the pharmaceutical industry and it’s application in pharmacy and drug administration. With an emphasis on patient care, clinical practice, and medication management, this course gives graduates the skills they need to play a crucial role in healthcare teams.

Pharm D coursecan be pursued by students who have completed school education, i.e 10+2 with physics, chemistry, Biology and Mathematics. The curriculum ensures that students acquire practical skills in addition to academic achievement by combining theoretical knowledge with practical experience in hospitals, community pharmacies, and research labs.

A Pharm D Degree opens numerous job options are available in clinical research, hospital pharmacies, the pharmaceutical industry, and patient counselling are made possible by pursuing a PharmD degree. Selecting the best Pharm D institutions in Uttar Pradesh guarantees access to high-quality instruction, hands-on training, and industry exposure for students who are passionate about enhancing healthcare outcomes. This equips graduates to succeed in the quickly expanding pharmacy and healthcare sectors.

Pharm. D Full Form

Pharm D stands for Doctor of Pharmacy. It is a six-year professional doctoral degree that focuses on students enrolled in this professional and prepares them for clinical positions within the healthcare industry. Pharm D has a strong emphasis on clinical practice and patient engagement, in contrast to B.Pharm, which is more industry- and production-focused. Regarding medication, consider it a link between the patient and the physician.

Pharm D Course Details

Pharm.D. (Doctor of Pharmacy) is a six-year professional doctoral degree, which consists of five years of university work and one year of hospital internship. The curriculum is based on clinical pharmacy, patient care and medication management training graduates to work in healthcare teams. The qualification usually includes the completion of 12th grade by encompassing Physics, Chemistry and either Biology or Math.

History and Global Recognition

Pharm D, which was first offered in India by the Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) in 2008, is based on the American model of pharmacy education and is regarded as the prerequisite degree for obtaining a pharmacy license. A PharmD is regarded as a clinical doctorate worldwide, particularly in the USA, Australia, and some regions of Europe, and its holders are permitted to work as patient-care pharmacists.

Pharm D: Course Structure

Pharm D's dual-entry pathway—a full 6-year program for new students and a shortened 3-year version for those with a B.Pharm—is one of its distinctive features.

Dissection of the Programs

1. 6 years of Pharm D (Regular)

Five years of coursework

One year of required hospital internship or clinical rotation

2. Three years of study plus a one-year clinical internship make up the Pharm D (Post Baccalaureate) program, which is intended for students who already have a Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm) degree.

Learning Methodology and Subjects

Among the many topics covered in the course are pharmacy and clinical pharmacy.

Hospital pharmacy; community pharmacy; pharmacotherapeutics; biostatistics and research methodology; patient safety and counseling

Working in multidisciplinary teams in hospital settings, presenting cases, and providing real-time patient care are all major components of the final year.

Students are important contributors to contemporary healthcare systems because they receive training in clinical decision-making, pharmacovigilance, and theoretical knowledge.

Pharm D Eligibility Criteria after 12th

Eligibility for admission in Pharm D. Prior to pursuing your career as a clinical pharmacist, you must fulfill a few prerequisites. They're fairly simple, so don't worry.

Eligibility for Education

In order to enroll in the six-year Pharm D program, you must have completed Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Mathematics as required topics in your 10+2 or equivalent.

Alternatively, you need to have earned a Pharmacy Diploma from an accredited institution.

Minimum Marks and Age

The minimum age is 17.

Minimum grades: In PCB/PCM, the minimum is typically 50% aggregate, though each college may have a slightly different cutoff point.

Pharm D Admission Process in India

A combination of entrance tests, merit-based shortlisting, and in-person interviews (at certain colleges) are required to get into a Pharm D program in India. Although it's not as ruthless as MBBS, competition is growing over time.

Exams for Entrance

State-level or university-specific entrance tests are the basis for admission to the majority of colleges.

NEET (accepted sometimes)

BITSAT, KEAM (Kerala), EAMCET (Andhra Pradesh and Telangana), and PUCET (Panjab University)

JSSU Admission Exam

On the other hand, a few of private universities also provide direct admission based on Class 12 results.

Selection Based on Merit

At Mangalayatan University the Admission is granted on a first-come, first-served basis or through merit lists created using Class 12 board scores in many public and private colleges. In general, those with a solid scientific background and high scores in biology/mathematics, chemistry, and physics stand a greater chance.

No, MBBS and PharmD are not interchangeable. PharmD professionals are clinical pharmacists who help with medication therapy and patient safety, whereas MBBS graduates are physicians.

Q2 - Can a PharmD graduate prescribe medicine?

No, Pharm D graduates cannot prescribe medicines.

Q3 - What is the salary of a Pharm D in India?

The entry-level Pharm D graduates may earn up to ?3 LPA to ?5 LPA depending upon their knowledge and the organization they are absorbed in.

Q4 - Which is better: Pharm D or B Pharmacy?

Pharm D or B Pharmacy, both the programmes are related to the pharmacy industry, but their course duration is different. In Pharm D you earn a doctorate degree after 6 years of study whereas B.Pharm is just a graduate degree.

(57) Abstract :

A bio-composite material and method for its preparation are disclosed. The material consists of coconut coir fibers treated with epoxy

resin and hardener, then mixed with an epoxy resin matrix to form a composite. This composite exhibits improved mechanical

properties, including hardness and load-weight ratio, surpassing those of aluminum alloys. The preparation involves a hand layup

technique, and adjustments in the fiber length allow for tailored mechanical properties. The material is eco-friendly and biodegradable.

(54) Title of the invention : GYM PULL DOWN MACHINE FOR ELECTRICITY GENERATION

:A63B0021000000, H02K0007180000,

(61) Patent of Addition

to Application Number

Address of Applicant :Mangalayatan University, Aligarh Uttar

Hathras ----------- -----------

“GYM PULL DOWN MACHINE FOR ELECTRICITY GENERATION” The present invention relates to a gym pull -down machine

that converts human mechanical energy into electrical energy. The gym-based power generation system, includes a gym pull-down

machine with a frame structure and a pull-down bar for users to perform exercises, a first shaft (Shaft-A) and a second shaft (Shaft-B)

mounted at the top of the frame structure in a parallel arrangement, a freewheel sprocket and chain drive system connecting the pull -

down bar to the first shaft (Shaft-A), a heavy-duty rickshaw pipe rim mounted on the first shaft (Shaft-A) to act as a flywheel, storing

and regulating the rotational energy, a DC dynamo connected to the flywheel by a cotton rope drive, wherein the rotational energy

from the flywheel is converted into electrical energy by the DC dynamo, and a charging circuit, including an IC, a capacitor,  and

diodes, to charge a battery using the electrical energy generated by the DC dynamo.

No. of Pages : 16 No. of Claims : 7

In-House Seminar on “Golden Ratio: Mathematics, Art and Nature”

Date: 29 June 2023

Venue: Shipra Block, Room Number 002

Timings: 10:00 am to 11:00 am

No. of Faculty and Students: 63

Speaker: Dr. Swati Agarwal, Assistant Professor (Mathematics)

About the Speaker:

Dr. Swati Agarwal earned her Ph.D. in Mathematics from Dayalbagh Educational Institute (Deemed University),

Agra and has accumulated more than four  years of teaching experience in the field. Her primary research interest lies

in Operations Research. She has published about 9 research articles in various international journals of repute and

holds 4 books to her credit. Dr. Agarwal has presented her research papers at over 10 national and international

conferences and has attended more than 15 workshops and FDPs. Furthermore, she has reviewed few research

articles for renowned journals such as Opsearch (Springer -Nature), Annals of Operations Research (Springer-Nature),

and International Journal of Systems Science (Taylor & Francis) . She is also a life member of several professional

bodies, including the Indian Science Congress, MathTech Thinking Foundation, International Association of

Engineers, etc.

About the Topic:

"The Golden Ratio," often represented by the Greek letter Phi (Φ), is a mathematical constant that has fascinated

mathematicians, artists, and scientists for centuries. It is a unique number that appears in various aspects of nature,

art, and architecture. This seminar delved into the mathematical properties of the Golden Ratio, its historical

significance, and its profound influence on aesthetics and design across different cultures and time periods.

Graphical representation of Golden Ratio and its application in Architecture

At its mathematical core, the Golden Ratio is defined as a number approximately equal to 1.6180339887. It emerges

from the solution to a simple algebraic equation, making it a key player in the world of mathematics. Understanding

its properties, such as the fact that Φ + 1 = Φ² (Phi squared), unveils its unique allure.

This seminar delved into the artistic realm, where the Golden Ratio has left an indelible mark. From ancient

civilizations to contemporary artists, the ratio's presence in art is undeniable. Attendees explore d how this ratio had

been used to create visually pleasing compositions, balanced and harmonious designs, and captivating artistic

Application of Golden Ratio in Art

The Golden Ratio isn't confined to human creations; it is deeply intertwined with the natural world. Participants

uncovered its prevalence in the spirals of seashells, the arrangements of sunflower seeds, and the proportions of

branches on trees. The seminar showcased how the Golden Ratio appears as a fundamental pattern in the DNA of

nature, adding to the awe-inspiring beauty and structure found in our environment.

This seminar on " Golden Ratio: Mathem atics, Art, and Nature" successfully  unlock the mysteries of this

mathematical constant and its multifaceted influence. Attendees were taken on an interdisciplinary journey that

blended historical insights, mathematical exploration, and captivating visual representations. As a result, participants

left the event with a deeper appreciation for the elegance and universality of the Golden Ratio. This seminar

effectively connected the dots between mathematics, art, and the natural world, demonstrating that the Golden Ratio

is more than just a number —it serves as a key to revealing the hidden symmetries and harmonies that grace our

Seminar Details:

The In-house Seminar on "The Golden Ratio: Mathematics, Art, and Nature" took place on 29th of August 2023, at

Shipra Block, Room Number 002, from 10:00 am to 11:00 am. The seminar was organized by the Institute of Applied

Sciences and was attracted a diverse audience, including 57 students from various academic disciplines such as B.Sc.,

B.Sc. B.Ed., and BCA and 06 faculty members.

The seminar  commenced with the introduction on the concept of  Golden Ratio and its mathematical definition.

Attendees were taken on a journey through history, exploring ho w this mathematical constant had  been employed by

artists and architects to create visually pleasing compositions. The seminar also examined the presence of the Golden

Ratio in the natural world, highlighting its prevalence in biological and physical phenomena.

Throughout the presentation, Dr. Agarwal provided numerous examples that showcased the practical applications of

the Golden Ratio in art and design, ranging from classical works of art to contemporary architectural masterpieces.

Attendees gained a deeper understanding of the aesthetic harmony and balance that the Golden Ratio can bring to

various forms of creative expression.

The seminar concluded with an engaging Q&A session, during which attendees had the opportunity to further explore

the topic and seek clarification on any aspects of the Golden Ratio that piqued their interest.

Seminar Lecture on “Golden Ratio: Mathematics, Art and Nature”

The In -House Seminar on "The Golden Ratio: Mathematics, Art, and Nature" proved to be an enlightening and

intellectually stimulating event. Dr. Agarwal 's expertise and passion for the subject left attendees with a profound

appreciation for the significance of the Golden Ratio in mathematics, art, and the natural world.

We extend our sin cere thanks to all the participants, including the students and faculty members for making this

seminar a valuable educational experience for all. We hope that the exploration of such interdisciplinary topics will

continue to enrich our institution's academic offerings, fostering a deeper understanding of the connections between

mathematics, art, and the natural world.

Event Coordinator                                                    HoD, IAS (Convenor)

Painting Demonstration and Lecture

"Mental-Consciousness and Expression in Painting".

Date: 14-06-2023

Time:  2PM -4PM

Venue: Shipra Block(Room no.506)

Speaker: Dr. Shivendra Singh

(Retd. Professor- Drawing & Painting)

Prof. Shivendra Singh is one of the leading Art Painter in India. He has served DEI, Agra as a faculty many years. He

has an illustrated career as an academician, demonstrator and research supervisor during his tenure as professor.

He is awarded by Out Standing Merit Sketching Award by Banaras Hindu University in 1972, Honoured for creative

work by Sanskar Bharti, Agra 1980,

A live demonstration-based guest lecture session on painting was held at M.U. smart classroom (Room no.506/

Shipra block) from 2 P.M. on 14-06-2023.

The primary objective to organize this lecture was to allow the participant students to become familiar with the

principles of painting and its various technical aspects and how to apply those theories on canvas in a practical

Eminent artist and academician Dr. Shivendra Singh was invited to conduct the Lecture - Demonstration session on

the topic " Mental-Consciousness and Expression in Painting".

In the beginning, Mr. Ajay Singh Rathore, Assistant Professor (visual art), welcomed and introduced the guest artist

with the students and teachers of DVPA.

Around 30 students and teachers attended this informative session which was ended through a question –answer

dialogue between artist and the students.

The guest artist and presenter was felicitated by Dr.Poonam Rani, HOD, DVPA with anAngVastra and memento.

Dr.Poonam Rani said that this type of workshop is very helpful for all the students. It develops confidence and

creativity. Pt. DebasisChakroborty, Sri Vilas Palkhe, Dr.RamkrishnaGhosh, Dr.Premlata, Mr. Ajay Singh and Mr.Uday

Kumar were also present.

At the beginning of the demonstration, Prof. Singh explained the various aspects of painting with live demonstration

and examples. He also advised the student that  the need for concentrating your subject matter is very much

required. Mental- Consciousness or self-observation is prime factor in a painting . He also emphasised that this

session is aimed at orienting one towards a

deeper outlook of the characteristics and detailing of the subject. Overall, the main focus should be to appreciate

the beauty of expression through the painting.

Conclusion:  We sincerely acknowledge the expertise and the unique presentation style of Prof. Shivendra Singh and

hope that this session has marked a deep-rooted thought process among students.

We are looking forward to organise more such interactive sessions under in -house initiatives.

methodology of Story Telling.In the second session on first day, Dr. Yatendra Pal, Dr. Kavita

Sharma, Dr. Anuradha Yadav and Dr. Sanjay Pal explained the use of Story telling in different

Kavita Sharma illustrated the use of Story Telling in Social Studies subject. Dr. Yatendra Pal

demonstrated the use of Story Telling in Science and Dr. Sanjay Pal explained how story Telling

can be used in specific topics of Biology.

The sessions were interactive. On the second day, students prepared illustrations and narrated

stories. Teacher trainees enjoyed this activity and asserted that this shall help them to engage

In the end, teachers appreciated the hard work put in by students and applauded them for giving

“Plastic Pollution and its impact on Environment”
