You can choose from a variety of jobs such as:JournalistA journalist is responsible for writing articles that are informative, interesting, and accurate. They write stories that inform the public about current events and issues. They interview newsmakers, fact check, and edit their own stories before publication. They have a solid understanding of the world, their community, and their profession.

Public Relation Specialist

Public relations specialists are responsible for promoting the image, reputation and products of a company, often to a targeted audience by using a variety of communication tools. The PR specialist at a company is often the first point of contact when a customer has a question, complaint or concern. Public relations specialists should be able to listen to customer concerns and thoughts and be able to effectively relay that information back to their employer.

The role of the screenwriter is to serve as the film's primary storyteller, creating a visual narrative that compliments the director's vision. They are responsible for creating the visual components of the film and the music.

Radio jockey or RJ is a role played by an individual or a group of people that play recorded music, provide entertainment, and advertise products or services through a radio station via a radio show. Radio jockeys may either talk on the radio in between songs or do voice-overs for radio commercials, also known as radio ads.

Art Directors are responsible for the visuals of a marketing campaign. They plan, organize and direct creative teams to create and manage print ads, direct mail pieces, and marketing collateral. They have to have a deep understanding of the product, competition, target market and business goals.

Cartoonists create the idea and design the cartoons. They are also a storyboard writer, who is in charge of bringing the story together to make sense and helping the other artists and animators with the storyboards. To make all of this possible, a great cartoonist must have a broad knowledge of many different things and be very creative.

Content writers can be found in numerous places such as in-house, outsourcing companies, freelancing services and at home. Content writers are writers who are responsible for writing product descriptions, articles, blogs and newsletters. To be a good content writer, one needs to have an excellent command of the language and also keep up to date with the latest innovations in the market.

An advertiser is the one who displays ads through various media like online, print, TV, radio, etc. Advertisers can place the ad in a variety of formats and platforms to convey the message to their customers. They are responsible for determining which format will be the most effective for their target audience.

TV Correspondent

A TV correspondent is a journalist who is employed mostly by television stations. The TV correspondent is responsible for reporting news. The TV correspondent is responsible for reporting news from the viewpoint of the station or station group. In addition to the on-the-scene reporting, TV correspondents also host the news programs.

A Film director is accountable for the overall creative vision of the film, from the script to the final product. They are responsible for leading the entire film production team. They take charge of the overall vision of the film, which includes the artistic and technical elements, including how the actors are to perform each role. They are ultimately responsible for every aspect of the final product, from casting to editing.

What is a BA LLB Degree?

The BA LLB is a five-yearlaw coursedegree that blends a bachelor's degree in arts with law. It is known as a dual-degree program. The curriculum involves disciplines like law, business, and arts. It is a program that is focused on the study of law and related issues. The study of law is based on the principles of business and commerce.

What is B Pharmacy Degree?

B Pharmacy is the acronym for Bachelor of Pharmacy. B Pharmacy is a prerequisite for students who wish to practice as a pharmacist as their major career. The B Pharmacy course is normally AICTE and PCI approved. It is a four-year bachelor's course that focuses on providing students with a detailed understanding of pharmaceuticals. You will learn about a range of concepts associated with drug compositions, dosages, pharmacological effects and more as a Pharmacy student.

Considering accurate knowledge of curative pharmaceuticals, as well as awareness of dosage and distribution, is critical nowadays, and theB Pharmacy courseaggressively growing in demand. The curriculum allows students to learn about drug analysis and experimentation, drug discovery, drug dispensing, quality management and monitoring, scientific regulation, and more.

The B Pharmacy degree is among the most attractive career-centric degrees, with extensive job opportunities in both the government and private sectors. Pursuing this degree is an excellent approach to breaking into a variety of industries, including medication, drug production and distribution, private clinic, commercial pharmacy, clinical research & trials, and conventional medical institutions, to name a few. Hence, it is recognized as one of the most appealing medical degrees owing to better career advancement, accolades, rewards, and credibility as a professional.

What is the Scope of a B Pharmacy Degree?

Pharmacy has great future potential. B Pharmacy is a job-centric course in India that opens pathways for numerous career avenues. Being a doctor or nurse is no more the only respectable career alternative in the healthcare system, as they were in past few years. Presently, aB Pharmacy courseis a vital element that deals with numerous facets of the healthcare business as a whole. It is a well-known and trustworthy profession where aspirants can find potential employment options with competitive salaries. The domestic market is expected to rise threefold in ten years, according to India's Economic Survey 2021.

Despite the industry's mounting issues, 58,000 new employments are predicted to be generated by 2025, as the business is anticipated to rise by 45%. After course completion, professionals can work for the government, or pharmaceutical firms, or even establish their own pharmacy. This degree would open too many employment options in India and abroad.

There will be several career prospects in areas such as therapeutics and medicines, drug design & development, clinical medicine, pharmaceutical technology, merchandising, quality assurance, and manufacturing and many more. After finishing the B Pharmacy degree, students can pursue the Master of Pharmacy (M Pharm) degree if they wish to continue their education.

Top 16 Best Jobs Opportunities after B Pharmacy Degree

The massive influx of job opportunities has resulted in an upsurge in career prospects in the pharmacy profession over the years. The future of pharmacy is highly promising. B Pharmacy professionals can get employment in both government and private organisations. You can easily seek jobs after completing your degree in top job profiles such as-

1. Analytical Chemist

Large manufacturers always rely on analytical chemists. The primary responsibility of an analytical chemist is to do research and develop new instruments, techniques and solutions for real-world applications. Analytical chemists also analyse chemicals and materials for use in consumer products, medicine, research and government. These chemists measure the composition of mixtures of chemicals and materials, including in water and soil samples and biological tissue.

Analytical chemists strive to understand how chemicals react with one another and the environment and at the same time they research to develop new tools and techniques to protect human health and the environment. Analytical chemists also use their knowledge of analysing chemicals for alternative energy sources, such as biomass and ethanol.

2. Food and Drug Inspector

Food and Drug Inspectors' primary duty is to inspect food and pharmaceutical products. The roles and responsibilities of a Food and Drug Inspector are quite extensive. They inspect the establishments and products (raw material, finished goods, packaging material and equipment) that fall under the jurisdiction of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act. Food and Drug Inspectors usually work for the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of the concerned state government. Food and Drug Inspectors ensure that the manufacturing process is properly done, all food products in the market are produced and marketed hygienically and all the chemicals used are safe for human consumption. This makes sure that the food sold in the market is safe for people to consume.

Inspectors verify the quality of the food produced, the quantity, where the food is produced, how it is produced and the processing technique. Inspectors also make sure that the food produced is stored and marketed at the right temperature and for the right periods.

3. Hospital Drug Coordinator

Hospital drug coordinators are responsible for coordinating patient drug orders and supplies in a clinical setting. They also manage a patient's drug therapies and ensure that they receive proper medication. The drug coordinator also handles drug recalls, drug shortages, and drug insurance issues and maintains records and inventory.

Additionally, they are responsible for the purchasing, storage, and dispensing of medications and ensuring that they are available to the hospital staff when needed.

4. Drug Therapist

A drug Therapist is a kind of therapist who treats addiction and substance abuse disorder. The drug therapist helps his patients in the process of recovery and sets up a program of treatment to help them recover. In the treatment program, he sets up the stages of clinical intervention, which normally starts with detoxification and ends with relapse prevention. The drug therapist also helps his patients to set up the right kind of support system and assists them with the psychological issues that they face, helping patients to stay away from drugs. Drug Therapists do drug counselling and maintain the proper environment for patients. They also keep proper records of the patient and the drugs used. They also keep updating the patient with all the new developments that happened in the medical field.

5. Chemical Technician

The principal role of a chemical technician is to carry out chemical process operations and help to ensure that all processes are carried out safely and reliably. Chemical technicians use scientific knowledge to solve problems in the chemical, food, and pharmaceutical industries. They test air, water, soil, and many other substances to ensure the quality of the air, water, soil, and many other substances to ensure the quality of the products we consume every day.

Usually, they work in production and quality control in these industries. Their tasks include testing and maintaining equipment, and collecting, preparing, packaging, and storing materials. They also design and develop new ways to improve manufacturing processes and create new products. In later stages, they examine and analyse samples to ensure that products are safe for human or animal use.

6. Drug Technician

A drug technician is a professional who is involved in the preparation, compounding, and dispensing of medicines to patients. They are employed in hospitals, pharmacies, ambulatory surgical centres, nursing homes, and dialysis units. The drug technicians are specially trained to do roles like care of equipment, operation of equipment, maintenance and calibration of equipment, etc. They are responsible to make sure that the lab is updated with new technology, new equipment and apparel.

The job of a drug technician is to prepare, compound and dispense drugs as per the prescription of a physician. When preparing a drug for a patient, a drug technician uses precision measurements and implements sanitation measures to ensure the drug's purity. A drug technician is not only responsible for dispensing drugs in a hospital or pharmacy; they may also mix compounds for patients requiring intravenous drugs. In addition to preparing and dispensing drugs, a drug technician may also review and evaluate the following records of patients: medication, vaccination and treatment compliance.

7. Drug Inspector

A drug inspector, who also goes by the name of a pharmaceutical inspector, is responsible to ensure that the medicines and drugs that are manufactured and sold in the country are safe for use. They are responsible to ensure that the products are not adulterated, impure or expired. A drug inspector is responsible to keep a check on the quality of the drug and its purity. They may also be responsible for the security and safety of their company’s assets. Inspectors ensure that the company maintains its high standards of quality. They make sure that the company’s assets are treated carefully and safely.

Drug inspectors may also be required to personally test drugs to make sure that they meet proper standards and are not contaminated.   Drug inspectors come in different varieties. Inspecting the facilities is only part of the job. They are also responsible for ensuring that those that work in the facilities can do their jobs safely. This includes monitoring the facilities and ensuring that there are proper security measures for protecting the products and the workers.

8. Health Inspector

Health inspectors hold a variety of roles in the public health sector. Their main responsibility is to protect the general public from health hazards. Their main responsibilities are to ensure public safety and check food facility conditions, write reports and educate businesses to maintain the highest possible standards.

Health Inspector is the one who has the responsibility to inspect the food quality and health services. He will inspect all the food sources, restaurants and food-processing plants, and the food products. He also checks the water supply, sewage system and the arrangement of all the food preparation and ensures that they are maintaining safe and clean conditions. Finally, they will check the food-handling procedures and any other things related to the health services in restaurants.

Being a pharmacist, you will always be the first to know about an individual’s health. You are not only responsible for the quality of the medicines dispensed but also for maintaining the cleanliness of the store, ensuring that all staff is trained to handle and dispense the medications correctly. With an ever-growing demand for medicines, pharmacists are expected to have a deep knowledge of medicines.   A pharmacist is a health care practitioner with expertise in drug therapy.

A Pharmacist is responsible to inspect, identify, measure, testing and dispensing the most appropriate medicines and drugs to the patients. They also dispense medications, help in maintaining the inventory and are further involved in counselling patients about their medications to ensure the safe and effective use of the medicines.

10. Research Officer

The research officer is a key position in the industry. The research officer is usually a very experienced person with a lot of knowledge. Research officers are responsible to oversee several different things, depending on whatever research service they’re working for. They have to collect information, define and suggest objectives, track the progress of the research, conduct a study, present the findings, and publish these results. This will include doing complex mathematics and statistical analysis, keeping track of the equity and debt portfolios and doing detailed research on corporate structures and the companies which are traded in the market.

Apart from these, they are responsible to make sure that their research goes without any conflict of interest and ethical issues.

11. Pathological Lab Scientist

Pathological laboratory scientists are primarily focused to analyse a tissue sample from a patient, diagnose the disease involved, and determine the proper course of action for treatment. They also provide information about the likely progression and best treatment for a disease. Pathologists are employed by hospitals, laboratories, biotechnology companies, universities and government agencies.   The Pathologist must have an understanding of a large number of diseases to properly identify the disease and the specific clinical history of the patient to be able to determine the best treatment.

12. Research & Development Executive

Research and Development Executives are responsible for the development of new products and the improvement of existing products. One is accountable for all new product development activities and their timely completion. An individual is responsible to develop a new product and cost estimate. R&D executive is responsible to communicate and coordinate with all company personnel to create a product, process, and service innovations. They are also in charge of leading and/or participating in the development of technical research projects that involve the application of expertise and solutions to business problems.

13. Making Prescriptions to Patients

The prescription is the final output of the practitioner and it is his responsibility to write it correctly as it is the most important legal document in medical practice. Prescribing Medications is the most important consideration for a healthcare provider when prescribing medication in the best interest of the patient. When medications are prescribed, the provider must consider the potential benefits, adverse effects and potential interactions of the medications. They also need to consider the patient’s medical history, lifestyle, and physical condition. They must also monitor a patient’s response to the medication.

14.Medical Writer

Medical Writer's role is to write or help write medical and health-related content, including educational materials and reference sources, for distribution to customers. Medical writing is a challenging career for many various reasons, including-

(a) the ability to communicate effectively

(b) the ability to use medical terminology accurately without misconstruing it and

(c) the ability to interpret complex medical concepts to a non-medical audience.

Additionally, creating medical documents is often a collaborative effort requiring medical writers to work closely with other healthcare professionals, so communication skills are essential. Hence, Medical Writers need medical knowledge and advanced skills in writing, editing, and web-based content management. Their work is almost entirely done in-house rather than in an outside medical writing firm.

15. Clinical Researcher

A clinical researcher is a healthcare professional who researches patients using experimental drugs and therapies. A clinical researcher mostly works in hospitals, clinical research centres and academic institutions. The highest percentage of clinical researchers are employed in the hospital setting. In addition to using experimental drugs and therapies, clinical researchers also work on new drugs and pharmaceutical products by doing clinical trials. The work of clinical researchers is very essential in the medical field. The main objective of clinical researchers is to save the lives of patients by improving healthcare.

16. Medical Representative

Medical Representatives are the face and voice of the company with which they are affiliated. They are the most important person in the healthcare industry. They are the first and most important contact a doctor or patient has with the company they work for. The Medical Representative sells medical devices, instruments and medicines to the medical practitioners in hospitals. A medical representative's job involves contacting doctors and healthcare practitioners and conveying information to them about a particular medical product. The medical representative meets healthcare practitioners at medical conferences and expos, and also visits their hospitals and offices. The job also involves providing detailed information about the product to the physician by organizing medical conferences, seminars and workshops.   Medical Representatives conduct business with customer service, sales and marketing skills, and must be able to learn relatively quickly.

Medical Representatives need to have excellent communication and presentation skills, as well as computer skills to use a CRM, tracking and charting software.

This course is of three years duration and offers full information about the working of a surgery room, its equipment and the human anatomy. B.Vocin Operation Theatre Technology professionals are in charge of the planning and preparation that must be decided to make in the operation theatre before and after the surgical procedures are executed.

These include looking after all surgical equipment, disinfecting them, and preparing the dressing table, operation theatre table, instrument table and anaesthesia table. They also manage the medications required for surgery, as well as anaesthesia gases, drapes, and all linen, as well as their decontamination. They bring together sterile and non-sterile tools while also regulating them to ensure that they are all working properly. They also help with specialized procedures like endoscopic surgery, laparoscopic surgery, joint replacements, digital angiograms, and lithotripsy, among others.

B.Voc in Operation Theatre Technology Course Objectives

The curriculum is designed to give students a sound understanding of safety standards and practices.

The main aim of this course is to provide skills required for working in a medical environment for various medical treatments or surgeries.

The course aims at equipping students with the requisite knowledge and skills to manage theatres and ICUs in hospitals.

The students of this course will be trained in a variety of medical, surgical and administrative skills that are required to be a part of the hospital management team.

The bachelor's degree is intended to teach students various techniques used in a surgical procedure, including disinfection and sterilization.

The course will help you to understand the basic medical and surgical procedures and equip you with certain skills that you will need to apply in a real-world scenario.

Lab technicians hold a very important role in any medical environment. The lab technician is extremely important to the doctor and his or her staff. A lab technician is responsible for ensuring that the lab is running smoothly and efficiently. They maintain and handle the lab operations. Laboratory technicians often assist the doctor with diagnosing conditions, determining the source of a patient's illness, and developing a treatment plan.

Anaesthetist Consultant

The responsibilities of an anaesthetist consultant vary by speciality and vary by country. Anaesthetists are the doctors who administer anaesthesia and monitor a patient's condition during surgery. They are the ones keeping a patient safe while the surgeons are cutting the body open and treating the illness. During an operation, they are responsible for supplying the proper level and dosage of anaesthesia to the patient. Anaesthetists are often the unsung heroes when it comes to surgeries as they are usually behind the scene.

Associate Consultant

As an OT Associate Consultant, you will learn how to support the OT department and help with OT procedures and patient care. Client services are their primary responsibility.

The OT professionals are considered the backbone of the system. The operation theatre technician is responsible for the smooth and proper running of the operation theatre. He or she should aware of the procedures to be followed before and after the operation to prevent any untoward cases. Also, they are responsible for the cleanliness and safety of the operation theatre, must be able to monitor the surgery room to make sure that the equipment and the room are safe and monitor and maintain the temperature, humidity and pressure of the operation theatre.

A perfusionist is someone who is in charge of all the machines in an operation. A perfusionist ensures that all of the equipment, tools and machines in the operating theatre are in place and in running condition. BAMS Full Form in Medical

What is a BAMS Degree Course?

As mentioned above, Ayurveda is one of the world's oldest medical systems. The Ayurvedic healthcare system is founded on the notion that Ayurvedic medication enhances the body's innate healing potential. The Ayurvedic approach is a reliable medicinal approach for treating, preventing, and revitalizing. Minimizing symptoms, clearing impurities, eliminating anxiety, strengthening illness resistance, and increasing patient life harmony are all aspects of Ayurvedic therapy.

BAMS Admission is a Bachelor’s Degree Course offered in India. It is a full-time 4+ years + 1-year internship course on Ayurveda, the holistic and ancient branch of medicine that focuses on preventive and curative health care. Ayurveda involves nutrition and lifestyle, herbal therapy, surgery and yoga. A BAMS degree course will teach you how to diagnose and cure people of various diseases. Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) Course Objectives

The objectives of the BAMS are-

The goal of the Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) course is to provide the candidate with complete and comprehensive instruction in many elements of Ayurveda.

To introduce the student to the basic Ayurvedic principles and techniques of understanding the body, its functions, maintenance and wellbeing.

Comprehend the importance of Ayurvedic principles in the context of societal health issues.

Based on the clinical evaluation and suitably identified and executed investigations, be able to diagnose and control acute and chronic disorders.

Will become competent to accomplish effective Ayurvedic care of all kinds of illness after promptly examining the patient and assimilating existing clinical and research evidence to establish the entirety of ailments.

To equip the students with knowledge of different diseases and to demonstrate the principles of management of these diseases in view of current medical practices.

Should become able to critically evaluate pertinent research literature and apply it to influence Ayurvedic therapy.

Ensure continued expertise and the latest breakthroughs in the field by self-study.

To just be capable of recognizing and caring for socioeconomic, ecological, anatomical, and psychological determinants of health in a given instance while developing curative, therapeutic, and preventive measures.

To impart training in the principles and techniques of modern Medicine and Surgery for a better understanding of the management of life-threatening conditions and for postgraduate studies.

Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) Course Duration

BAMS (Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) is the first degree in the Ayurvedic medical and surgical system, which has been treating humanity for thousands of years. The duration of this course is around 4.5 years plus a 1-year internship with live practical exposure.

The most basic criteria for admission to the BAMS course is qualifying for the 10+2 examination in a science stream. In 12th grade, the candidate should score 50% in disciplines such as physics, chemistry, and biology.

The candidate must pass a national level entrance examination, such as NEET (National Eligibility Cum Entrance Test).

The candidate is chosen based on a standardized counselling process and overall merit, which is computed using the total number of points gained in the qualifying examination (12th grade) and the cut-off points obtained in the admission exams.

After NEET, BAMS applicants would be able to get a centralised counselling notification to choose a college based on their scores. Colleges can next arrange a personal interview round to further filter down the candidates.

Top 12 Career or Job Opportunities after Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery

For graduates in diverse sectors of medicine, the BAMS programme opens up many prospects and possibilities. BAMS graduates can find work in a variety of fields, including healthcare, education, drug manufacturing and distribution, research, and management. Following are some examples of career opportunities that can be pursued after graduating with a BAMS degree:

1. Ayurvedic Doctor -

An Ayurvedic doctor works as a consultant for health, wellness and medicine. The doctor can also prescribe exercises, diets, and other lifestyle changes.

2. Ayurvedic Physician -

A good Ayurvedic physician should be the one who is well-trained and capable of identifying and curing the disease or disorder. He is the one who has studied Ayurveda and uses the principles of this medical system as part of the process of diagnosing and treating illness.

A professor should have a vast knowledge of Ayurveda. He should be well-educated and trained. A good professor has a thorough understanding of the topics that he is teaching. In addition, he is a reliable resource for students and an example of the Ayurvedic way of life. With his positive attitude, a professor can inspire students to learn new things with confidence.

An Ayurvedic therapist is a health professional who helps patients deal with their illnesses by applying the principles of Ayurvedic medicine. He is trained to identify the root cause of an illness and offer the most effective long-term treatment to help cure the condition.

5. Medical Representative-

An Ayurvedic Medical Representative is an important person for promoting Ayurveda as well as for resolving the doubts of people about Ayurveda. He is a professional having knowledge of Ayurveda and herbal products, and should possess marketing skills for promoting Ayurvedic products. He should be able to identify the market potential of Ayurvedic products and should be able to create demand in the market.

6. Pharmacist -

The Ayurvedic Medical Pharmacist plays a very important role in the Ayurvedic system of medicine. An Ayurvedic Medical Pharmacist also handles the preparation, distribution and storage of the various forms of medicines prescribed by the Ayurvedic Physician. Their role also includes helping the patient choose the right medicine to suit his/her condition and health. Finally, they also counsel the best practices to maintain and preserve the medicinal properties of Ayurvedic medicines.

7. Clinical Trials Coordinator-

The ayurvedic clinical trials coordinator helps in carrying out the clinical trial procedures and safety standards. He is in charge of the Ayurvedic medicine and the task carried out by the clinical trial coordinator is to ensure that the clinical trial is completed in a legitimate manner.

8. Medical Officer Scientist-

An Ayurvedic Medical Officer Scientist is primarily responsible for the production and supply of good-quality medicine. They are also responsible for testing new drug formulations, preparation of injectable and oral formulations, isolation and purification of various drugs from the various raw materials, standardization of drugs and formulations, preparation of labelling, and detailed packing are the essential tasks.

9. Research Assistant-

The Ayurvedic Resident is responsible for the treatment of patients and other health care professionals under the supervision of a licensed physician and provides support to the physician or governing body with the development, maintenance and reporting of the internal quality assurance program.

10. Product Manager-

Ayurvedic product managers are responsible for all the activities related to marketing and product management like Product planning, product introduction, product promotion, product launch, product visibility, product portfolio management, product pricing, and product portfolio tracking.

11. Business Development Officer-

Ayurvedic business development officers are employees of both Ayurvedic companies and Ayurvedic educational institutions, who act as a bridge between the producers and the consumers. He is a specialised sales executive with specific training and experience in Business development. He develops business opportunities by identifying potential customers, matching products & services offered by the company with their requirements, persuading them to use the company's products or services, and maintaining a relationship with them

12. Assistant Claims Manager -

Ayurvedic Assistant claims manager has to assist the claim manager to provide administrative support in managing the healthcare claims of their customers. The claim manager is responsible for ensuring that claims are processed in accordance with the company's policies and procedures. He must also ensure that all claim files are kept secure and up to date.

What is BA LLB Degree All About?

BA LLB course is one of the most prominent degree programs. BA LLB is a five-year law degree course. The degree is a combination of Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Laws, which are two highly different degree courses. The course is offered by the colleges affiliated with the General Council Bar of India. The degree is commonly known as BA LLB.

The BA LLB degree is designed to offer basic knowledge and train students inall aspects of the law and arts. It prepares students for a career in law,Government and non-Government services, private practice and research or alegal professional.

The program focuses on the learning andapplication of various disciplines such as communication skills, writing, andresearch. Here are the Top 10 Job opportunities for a BA LLB Degree Holder-

1. Legal Secretary -

This is one of the common positions for a BA LLB degreeholder in India. It is one of the most sought-after positions, especially ifyou have a law firm as your employer. The role of legal secretaries isessential for the smooth functioning of the legal system. A legal secretaryneeds to pay specialattention to detail, have excellent communication skillsand have a good grasp of legal terminology.

A Legal Secretary is an executive secretary whoperforms law firm support functions such as reviewing correspondence, preparingcase files and conducting research. Legal Secretaries are responsible for theintake of clients and their cases. In addition, they are responsible forkeeping client information and case information confidential. Specificresponsibilities of legal secretaries include making appointments, screeningand routing a call, taking shorthand and typing dictation, as well as filing.Some of the responsibilities of a legal secretary also include maintainingattorney calendars and drafting correspondences.

Any person who has completed an LLB degree in Indiacan join law firms as a law clerk. A law clerk is an assistant to a judge or alawyer. In the United States, law clerks are called judicial clerks. Alaw clerk is often an attorney, and he or she may specialize in a specific areaof the law (such as tax or corporate law).

A law clerk is a research assistant whoassists a judge in the administration of justice. The job of a law clerkinvolves a lot of research and writing. Law clerks perform a variety of tasks,but their mainresponsibility is to conduct legal research and provideassistance to judges in the performance of their duties. They help the attorneydraft legal documents, prepare legal pleadings, precedents, and research andwrite briefs, opinions and memorandums. Besides, they also need to assist theattorney during the court trials and hearings. For this, they have to abide by theattorney’s instructions and directions.

3. Legal Associate/Advisor -

Legal associates are legal professionals who aresupervised by attorneys. A Legal Associate is alawyer that is a part of a lawfirm and helps the senior lawyers with legal and other professional matters.They are trained to help in providing all the administrative and legal supportthat a lawyer would need so that they can concentrate on cases. They can workin different departments, including litigation, corporate, tax and real estate.

Legal Associates also work under the supervision ofthe firm's Partners. They also share their experience and skills with Lawyerswho do not have any experience and are at the bottom of the hierarchicalladder. Legal Associates would also be able to advise the lawyer on thecases they are working on. At the same time, they would be able to analyse theimportance of these cases. Theyhelp lawyers by serving different clients. Theyalso take a significant part in preparing documents, legal briefs, etc.

4. Litigation Lawyer -

A litigation lawyer will be involved in variousstages of a legal dispute from the beginning to the end of the proceedings. Therole of a litigation lawyer is to understand what needs to be done to settle a dispute. Besides, their role will vary depending upon the area of law in which individual practice.The most important aspects of the job will includeconducting research, interacting and negotiating with clients, preparing forcourt proceedings and presenting arguments in court before a judge.

In most cases, litigation lawyers represent clientsin cases involving civil, criminal and administrative law. In somejurisdictions, a litigation lawyer may also perform the function of a publicprosecutor. For example, in the state of New York, a lawyer is eligible topractice as both a public prosecutor and a private lawyer.

A litigation lawyer must be able tointerpret the laws and understand how the case will be impacted by the factsand the law. They must be familiar with the relevant law; various court systemsand thejudges must know how to research the law and must be able to apply thelaw to the facts of the case. Other than that, a lawyer should keep track ofevery movement of the case. This is not easy if you are working with abig law firm. In addition to this, a lawyer should be skilful in writing and communicationwith the other party in the dispute.

5. Criminal Lawyer -

Criminal lawyers in India are the lawyer who handlescases related to crime. In India, any person can become a criminal lawyer. Butthey need to register themselves under the Bar Council of India.

Criminal lawyers are those who defend clientswho are accused of crimes. Their main job is to represent a person or business, whois charged with a crime in a court of law. They may also represent a defendantin a civil case, where compensation is claimed for damages. Theirprimary responsibility is to ensure the safetyof innocent people from false accusations. There are different types ofcategories of criminallawyers. The lawyer can be a junior criminal lawyer,senior criminal lawyer, criminal appeal lawyer, contract barrister andsolicitor etc.

Also, they offer legalassistance to the accused person by providing counsel and defence in criminalcourts. Other than that, they defend the client's rights under the law and mayargue that the charges against the client should be reduced or dropped.

6. Legal Analyst -

A Legal Analyst is an employee of a law firm whoperforms research and analysis on legal documents and cases. One is an expertin the law, who can understand and explain all the issues related to thelaw and its applications.

A legal analyst is not just restricted to analysing legal information but also plays a key role in facilitating the day-to-daybusiness activities. Their main objective is to understand the company'spresent position concerning the law and provide proposals or solutions tovarious legal issues. The legal analyst uses the available database and legalresearch tools to gather information about the company's legal obligations, analyse it and communicate theimplications and potential risks to management.They also suggest and implement changes by performing research, draftingcontracts and advising in policymaking.

However, in many other cases, a legal analyst actsas a liaison between the company and the law firm. It is the responsibility ofthe legal analyst to help the law firm to understand the client’s needs andtranslate them into legal terms. A legal analyst evaluates the case and guides the lawyers about the risks and the way forward.

7. Company Secretary -

A company secretary is an individual who isresponsible for the smooth functioning of the company and is the liabilityholder. They are responsible to ensure legal compliance and all the administrative tasks of the company. Some of theduties and responsibilities of the company secretary include Stock exchangecompliance, Corporate secretarial services, Tradeshow and exhibitionmanagement and also various other duties as per the requirement of the company.

Some of the other responsibilities include arrangingof Board Meetings as well as itsfunctions, understand the company's financialand business position as well as various factors that affect it, to managerelationships with the company's shareholders, banks and financial institutions, etc., managing the company's secretarial and administrativeduties, maintaining the company's corporate records, including share registers,minutes of the meeting of the shareholders, organizing the Board of Directorsmeetings, Audit Committee etc. Also,handling of legal affairs and duties of the company, ensuring thatall statutory obligations are fulfilled and all statutory documents areproduced as and when required.

Company Secretary is a vital postin any company. The responsibilities of a Company secretary are many,therefore, he or she should be a very experienced and skilled individual.

8. Legal Advisor -

A legal advisor is a professional who advisesbusiness transactions and transactions involving rights, contracts, and otherlegalities. The legal advisor is not only a legal expert but also a businessan advisor who advises on legal matters that are relevant to the businesstransaction.

A legal advisor is responsible for protecting andenforcing clients’ legal rights and interests. The role of a lawyer is toadvise you on what you should do in your future steps, depending on the problemyou have. They cannot make any decisions for you, but they can present you withall the pros and cons of your actions. For example, you are being sued by acustomer and your lawyer could help you get out of this situation by findingthe proper approach to dealingwith the situation. They help you understand theprocess of the lawsuit and they will help you prepare the quotes and documents.

Hence, the major role of a lawyer is to assist inmatters of law, be it litigation or contracts.They also advise on therelated aspects of business such as taxation, legal, labour and estate laws. They have to know the laws of the country and keep themselvesupdated with the latest amendments and enactments so that they can help theirclients in all possible ways.

Judge is a very important person in the IndianPolitical system. Judge is a person who has been carefully selected for anappointment as a judge of a court or other similar position by the President ofIndia. Judges help in protecting people’s rights and making sure that everyonegets a fair trial. A judge must be able to maintain impartiality and not takeinto account any outside influences such as personal relationships, religion,race, or politics.

The roles and responsibilities of a judge arenumerous. He or she is also responsible for making sure that all partiesinvolved also maintain a high level of respect and decorum and that no one isharassed or bullied. They are responsible for making the final decision and makingsure the rules of the game are being followed accurately.

In addition, a judge is mandated to uphold the last all times, but he or she is also encouraged to take into account individualcircumstances as well.

10. Paralegal -

A paralegal is a person licensed to work in thefield of law. He or she is a member of the legal team whoworks directly with the attorneys, rather than with clients. The mainresponsibility of a paralegal is to help the attorney with any aspect of legalwork. They may conduct research and gather information on cases, help developlegal documents such as complaints, motions, and briefs by researching relevantissues and authorities, provide assistance in legal research and writing,assist with client meetings, assist in officemanagement activities such asscheduling, filing, and answering phones, and other tasks as assigned.

Other responsibilities include providingadministrative support to attorneys and knowledge of legal coverages anddocuments. They may need to take and transcribe testimony and other legalevidence. Also, they analyse evidence and make recommendations to the attorney to help him come up with the best defence for the client.

who want to become a part of this legal world!

The selection process is conducted based on the college cut-offs and merits.

What is BTech Computer Science Degree All About?

Top 10 Career opportunities after BTech CSE

The computer science stream is very diverse. Students have a wide variety of career paths to choose from, some of which are more popular than others. Let's have a look at some of the top career options available after a BTech in Computer Science:ï»¿

1. Web Developer and Designer

The modern world is dominated by online commerce. Thus, companies need talented and creative web developers to maximize their online presence. B. Tech in Computer Science degree enhances student's practical skills, making them more capable candidates. Thereby, the scope of web development is relatively vast and the income potential is quite high.Likewise, web design plays a crucial role in attracting customers via websites. To compete effectively, business websites must be appealing, informative, and easy to understand. A web designer can either work as an employee or a freelancer. They earn well in either case.

2. Data Analyst and Data Scientist

Statistical data is collected and analysed by Data Analysts to make accurate predictions. Using this data, the company can then make informed decisions. Simultaneously, Data analysts are responsible for conducting full lifecycle analyses, which include requirements, activities, and designs. Developing analytical and reporting skills will be the responsibility of data analysts. In addition, they will track performance and quality control plans to identify areas for improvementTo determine how data can be used to achieve business goals, Data Scientists work closely with executives and stakeholders. Their jobs include designing data modelling processes, implementing algorithms, and creating predictive models to extract the data the business needs. They also help analyse the data and share their insights with colleagues.

3. Game Developer

Game developers develop all kinds of user interfaces and interfaces for computers, consoles, and other devices. An animation team, graphic artists, and designers will collaborate with you to create the game. A game must be completed within a set deadline and with a lot of efficiencies. Once you have the idea for a game, you must decide on the sound effects, the characters, and so on. Those who are good at coding and are creative might want to consider a career in game development.

4. System Database Administrator

Database administrators oversee and supervise software modifications, as well as keep track of customer purchases of the software. In such a position, you will need to be very watchful, and maintain control over the data bank, so that the confidential information is protected and secured as well.

5. Cybersecurity Specialist

Cyber security specialists are responsible for ensuring the security of software systems, networks, and data centres during the development stage. These specialists examine hardware and software components for vulnerabilities. They detect any attacks and monitor any intrusions. Their other responsibilities involve building firewalls into network infrastructure, carrying out counteractive protocols, and reporting incidents.

6. QA Engineer (Quality Analyst)

A QA specialist's role is to increase the quality of a software development process by finding and preventing defects before they occur. Their primary function is to assure quality. A quality assurance engineer works to prevent production defects and improve software development processes.

7. Software Developer/Engineer

Computer programmers create software, applications, and computer programs that are important across economic sectors. Code used by computer programs and applications is written and tested by programmers. They translate software designers' designs into code. Typically, they will update or extend existing code or test the code to find errors, fixing any faults that are found.

8. Mobile App Developer

A mobile app developer creates, tests, and develops applications for mobile devices using programming languages and development skills. In creating applications, they often take into account principles of design such as UI and UX. In addition to developing software for phone and tablet platforms, a mobile app developer is knowledgeable about mobile technologies.

9. Data Warehouse Analyst

Data is our most valuable asset in the digital economy, so protecting it becomes imperative. An IT security professional is responsible for protecting networks, infrastructure, and systems for businesses and organizations. The role of an information security professional is to assist business leaders in understanding and reducing cybersecurity risks.

10. Lecturer/Professor

If you have a knack in the teaching field, you can opt to become a lecturer or entry-level assistant professor in college, university or institute. All you need is good IT background qualifications and an advanced level of computer science skills and concepts.;

11. Banking & Government Jobs

The banking industry has proven to be an ideal choice for individuals who obtained ab tech engineering coursesin the Computer Science branch and are looking for a government job. Throughout the core banking solution, greater dependence on computers, and therefore the emergence of positions in computer science, has created a great need for talented people. Many banks published recruitment notices regarding the recruitment of IT officers under the category of Specialist Officers for numerous banking needs.

BHMCT Course Eligibility Criteria after 12th

Following their class 12, students can start taking BHM courses. For most colleges, the following are the eligibility requirements for taking a BHM course:

An average of at least 50% must have been achieved in the 10+2 class from a recognized board or equivalent.

You must possess at least a 50% score in your 3-year diploma in hotel management or equivalent to be considered for lateral entry admissions.

You must have studied English in your degree program.

Your communication skills should be excellent.

You must be between the ages of 19 and 22 (General Category). Candidates of SC and ST are allowed a 2–3-year age relaxation.

Bachelor of Hotel Management & Catering Technology? Admission Process

A majority of BHM admissions are merit-based based on the score obtained in the State or National-level entrance exams, but some colleges and institutes conduct their aptitude tests or, in a few cases permits direct admissions too.

Different modes of admission for the BHMCT Course are:

Entrance Exam Based Admission:

The majority of colleges administer admission tests at the college level, whereas some universities administer entrance exams at the national level. A candidate who passes the examination is invited to participate in counselling and group discussion rounds.

1. Merit-Based Admission:

Merit-based admissions are also available for BHM colleges. These colleges offer online and offline application options. Fill out the application form with your information, including your personal and educational details. Upon payment of the application fee, you will need to wait for the colleges to release the merit list.

2. Lateral Entry Admission:

Taking a course through the Lateral Entry pathway allows you to go straight into the second year of the course you selected. To be eligible for this, you must hold a diploma in the related field. Depending on the institute, you may need a 3-year diploma in hotel management or equivalent after you complete your 10+2.

BHMCT Course Fees in India

Well, depending upon the infrastructure and various facilities provided by the institute or university, the annual course structure might vary. But generally, Bachelor's of Hotel Management fees range between INR 3-10 Lakhs per year.

My goal as a healthcare professional is to improve access to medical services for underprivileged communities in society, making a difference in the world. In the future, I hope to volunteer in community clinics and remote areas where residents have no access to even basic healthcare facilities.

What are your strategies for handling stressful situations?

As far as managing stressful situations goes, I tend to do quite well. Initially, I analyze the situation to identify what I can control immediately. Following that, I formulate a strategy to put things back in order.

Despite the popularity of professional courses like engineering, medical, and CA; more and more youngsters these days are gravitating toward law because law as a profession not only offers lucrative career avenues but also the prestige and the power which adds with the profession is unmatched. A person who has excellent communication skills, power of argument, concrete critical thinking, and excellent analytical skills- legal sphere is the place to be. Therefore, the study of law has gained huge popularity and momentum.

With time the objective of law education has changed, there was a time when this academic field was meant to enlighten its practitioners, now one of the most sought out professions for those who wish to make it big. From becoming an advocate to occupying a superior position in organizations, a degree in law unlocks doors of flourishing careers and immense possibilities.

When it comes to pursuing a degree in law, one question that repeatedly haunts and creates confusion in every law aspirant is whether to choose a five-year integrated LLB or opt for a three-year LLB course. This blog aims to decode this dilemma and put forth an unambiguous answer, which will help students to take an informed decision.

Read Also -Scope and Career Opportunities after BA LLB Degree

What is Three-years Bachelor of Law (LLB)?

Bachelor of Law (LLB) is an undergraduate programme of three-years. Students who have completed graduation in any stream with 45% marks from any recognized University, he/she is eligible forLLB course admission.

The course lays stress on fundamentals of law, constitutions of India, Labour Law, Family Law, Human Rights & International Law, Administrative Law, etc. During three-years students are taught subjects, which are focused on law education.

The objective of the course is to impart an in-depth understanding of technical and doctrine aspects of the law and the role it plays in modern society.

Upon completion of the course, there is an option of higher studies like Master of Law (LLM).

Besides solid theoretical education, students go through rigorous practical education like courtroom practice as colleges layout Moot Courts, research submissions, Mock Trial Courts

Internship opportunities with top law firms, corporates, NGOs.

What is Five-years Integrated Bachelor of Law (BA LLB)?

Integrated Bachelor of Law is an undergraduate programme of five-years. Students who have completed 10+2 in any stream with 45% marks from any recognized board/ University, he/she is eligible forBA LLB admission.

Since it is an integrated programme, it covers subjects like History, Political Science, Economics, Sociology, etc. along with in-depth study of law and legislature.

The objective of this integratedlaw courseprogramme is to enlighten students with the socio-legal facets of the law. The course equips students with argumentative skills, and excellent analytical skills, which enable them to understand the relationship between law and society.

Compare to three-years LLB programme, the five-years integrated law programme provides comprehensive exposure to legal education. Students get early access to courtroom practice like moot courts, research submissions, mock trials, etc. Besides, students also undergo internships every semester with top law firms, corporates, NGOs, etc.

After completing the course, students can go for higher studies like LLM, MBA, Company Secretary, etc.

Major Curriculum of BA LLB:

Administrative Law, International Law, Labour Laws, Tax Laws, Corporate Laws, Civil law, Criminal law, Patent law, Banking and Insurance Law, Business Law, Intellectual Property Rights, International Economic Law, Political Science, Sociology, Economics, Direct & Indirect Taxes, Human Rights Law, History (Indian and World History), etc.

Major Curriculum of LLB:

Labour Law, Family Law, Constitutional Law, Human Rights & International Law, Environmental Law, Company Law, Legal Writing, Administrative Law, etc.

The Core Differences Between LLB And BA LLB:

BA LLB course is career-oriented, it is a comprehensive programme that includes case studies, mock court drills, etc. to make the study more practical and interesting. Whereas LLB course is focused on theoretical aspects, and students get less exposure to practical aspects of the law.

BA LLB covers law subjects along with arts subjects whereas LLB solely focused on the study of the law and related subjects.

Since BA LLB is an integrated programme, by studying same aspirants get a dual degree whereas by studying LLB they get a single degree.

Employment areas after BA LLB are Consultancies, Educational Institutes, Business Houses, Revenue Departments, News Channels, Sales Tax, and Excise Departments, Banks, Judiciary/Courts, etc. And employment areas after LLB are Colleges & Universities, Courts & Judiciary, Law Firms, MNCs, Bank (Legal Dept.)

Career Scope of Degree in Law (LLB/BA LLB):

Both courses unlock doors of equal opportunities, below are some popular careers after law degree.

Advocate is the most popular career option after degree in law. Yes! the power of the black coat can’t be ignored. With lucrative income, an advocate enjoys immense power and prestige.

One can make career as a legal advisor after law degree. A legal advisor is a law professional who provides legal advice to his or her clients.

One can appear in judicial services exams to become a magistrate and judge. The judge holds the highest authority in court and makes decisions after the hearing of a case in the court. Generally, judicial service exams are conducted by respective high courts of different states to fill the vacancies available.

Have you ever thought that a law professional can join the Indian Army? Not as a trooper on the field, but as a law professional. Yes, the Indian Army has a separate legal department known as the Judge Advocate Legal Branch. This department has legally qualified officers who take care of all legal issues for the army.

Corporate world can’t function without lawyers. In Corporate sectors, there is always a need for dexterous corporate lawyers to tackle legal issues. Therefore, after a law degree, one can make a career as a corporate lawyer.

In India, the media sector is flourishing leaps and bounds. The glamour, dazzle, power, prominence, and money in the media sector are fascinating today’s youth to make a magnificent career in this field. To make a career in media after 10+2, there are two popular professional undergraduate courses, BA Mass Communication and BA Journalism.

Both courses are highly similar in nature and sometimes mistaken to be synonymous. Therefore, maximum students don’t understand the core differences between these two courses. If you also have wondered about the difference between BA Mass Communication and BA Journalism, then this post is for you.

Through this post, we will discuss about major differences between BA Mass Communication course and BA Journalism course on the basic tenets of the core focus area, generic syllabus, and career opportunities.

What is BA Mass Communication degree?

First of all, let’s understand the term mass communication. Simply put, mass communication is the process of communicating with the masses. Anything and everything that involves reaching out to a large number of audiences come under the umbrella of mass communication. Mass Communication is a comprehensive field includes a fusion of advertising, public relation, photography, media practices, film making, entertainment industry, content writing, social media management, etc.

BA Mass Communicationdegree prepares students to interact with various media platforms to create and manage content that reaches to a large number of audiences.

BJMC courseimparts a comprehensive understanding of several domains of media including theater, radio, T.V., filmmaking, journalism, advertising, public relation, and digital media.

What is BA Journalism degree?

Unlike Mass Communication, Journalism is the practice of communicating news to people, be it in any strata- politics, economics, business, science, sports, or entertainment news. The job responsibility of a Journalist is gathering the data or news, editing it, validating the data or news with facts and pictures, and then broadcasting it in the most appropriate way through print media and electronic media. Where newspapers and magazines come under the purview of print media the same TV, Radio, and Internet lie under the electronic media.

BA Journalism degree prepares students in basic journalism practices and ethics.

The objective of BA Journalism is to prepare students to work on the fields and behind the desk for news media houses.

After completing the BA Journalism course, a student becomes efficient in identifying news and disseminating it in an appealing way.

BA Mass Communication vs. BA Journalism: Difference in Core Focus Area and Curriculum

Major Curriculum of BA Mass Communication:

Science of communication, Sociology, Principles of writing, Computer Applications, Psychology, Communication Technology, Political Science, News Writing, Reporting & Editing, Media Laws and Ethics, Advertising, Global Media, Communication Research, Public Relations, etc.

Major Curriculum of BA Journalism:

Introduction to Journalism, Reporting and Feature Writing, Editing, Press Laws & Ethics, Magazine & Niche Journalism, Broadcast Journalism, Photojournalism, Indian Regional Journalism, etc.

The Core Difference Between BA Mass Communication and BA Journalism.

The structure of the course:

BA Journalism course mainly involves the components of political science, economics, communication theory, history of journalism, and research methodology. The objective of the programme is to acquaint students with the social facts, media ethics, theoretical framework, and the role of media in society and country. On the other hand, BA Mass Communication course unlocks the doors of range of opportunities. It is a comprehensive programme, where students get acquainted with different media platforms like radio, TV, news, magazines, Internet, social media, films. etc. While pursuing mass communication course students learn the art of disseminating information in an interactive and engaging manner, which captivates a large number of audiences. Besides, the course equips students with the highest level of creativity, excellent writing skills, and communication skills.

Type of content conveyed:

Journalism is focused on stating facts without any manipulation. On the other side mass communication is the art of disseminating information through various media platforms. The type of content in mass communication can be promotional as well as non-promotional. But in journalism, there is no place for promotional or spicy content.

Scope of creative freedom:

There is no place for showing creativity in journalism, a Journalist only deals with facts. On the other side, in the field of mass communication, a person has more choice and freedom to display his/her creativity.

Employment opportunities:

In a broad sense, journalism is all about news reporting, news analysis, news anchoring, and news editing. The employment opportunities after BA Journalism are limited to news agencies, electronic media, print media, online media, and news portals. Undoubtedly, there is a lot of glamour, power, prominence, and money in the journalism profession but on the other side, there is a lot of struggle, challenge, and pressure in this profession. Journalism is not 9-5 desk job, here work-life balance and salary can be the cause of frustration.

On the other side, there is no dearth of opportunities afterBA Mass Communication course. After completing course, a person can find employment opportunities in several fields like NGOs, public relations and advertising agencies, corporate communication, communication solution organizations, UN organizations, media academics, content writing, photography, etc. Mass Communication field allows a person to express his/her creativity, thought, and ideas; thereby career in this field is not only well-paid rather career satisfaction is also very high.

News Anchor, News Reporter, News Editor, News Analyst, Photojournalist.

Job profile after BA Mass Communication:

Advertisement and Branding, Film Making, Video Editing, Photography, Public Relations, Radio Jockey, Video Jockey, Journalism, Content Writing and Development, Event Management, Wedding Planning, Creative Direction, Sound Mixing and Recording.

BCA Vs. B.Sc. Computer Science, Which Course is Better to Make A Successful Career in The Sphere of Information Technology.

After 10+2 in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics; maximum students want to pursue education programme related to computer. When it comes to choosing a suitable computer course after 10+2, then B. Tech Computer Science comes as the first choice. But, due to difficult curriculum, fierce competition, and high fees, many students don’t want to pursue B. Tech CS. Apart from B. Tech CS, there are few other undergraduate programmes related computer, which offer excellent scope in the matter of employment opportunities and higher studies. Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA) and B.sc Computer Science are two undergraduate courses, which opens the doors of successful career in the sphere of information technology.

But it is often found that student often remains in dilemmas between BCA and B.sc Computer Science. Because, in the matter of curriculum, higher studies, and employment opportunities both courses offer almost similar scope. To decode this dilemma, we will discuss each of these academic programmes individually evaluating their core focus area, generic syllabus and market value followed by a comparative analysis between them.

What is Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA)

Bachelor of Computer Application coursesis an undergraduate programme of three years, focused on the application of Computer Science.

Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA) imparts a holistic understanding of Internet technologies, web development, and mobile application development.

Being a practical education programme, BCA lays stress on programming language like C & C++, business communication, software engineering, networking, e-commerce, and, multimedia systems.

Upon Completion of Bachelor of Computer Application (BCA), students can go for Master of Computer Application (MCA).

BCA is a prestigious degree and it is accepted and recognized in all Indian Universities and government organizations.

Since BCA is an employment-oriented and practical education programme, thereby after completing the course students can find decent employment opportunities quickly, according to their skills and interest.

What is Bachelor of Computer Science (B.sc. CS)

Bachelor of Computer Science (B.sc. CS) is an undergraduate programme of three years, focused on the core concept of computer science.

Bachelor of Computer Science (B.sc. CS) imparts holistic understanding of mathematical foundation for computer science, computer fundamentals and architecture, data structures and C Programming.

It is a theoretical education programme, B.sc Computer Science lays stress on mathematical aspects in computer science, concept of programming, statistics, and electronic.

Higher education opportunities are Master of Computer Application (MCA), Master of Computer Science (M.sc CS), and B. Tech Computer Science.

Bachelor of Computer Science (B.sc CS) is a prestigious degree, and it is accepted and recognized in all Indian Universities and government organizations.

Since B.sc Computer Science (B.sc CS) is a concept-oriented and theoretical education programme, thereby the programme is suitable for higher studies and academics. Don’t expect any decent employment opportunity right after completing the course.

The objective of the BCA programme is to prepare students with a challenging role in the futuristic industry. Bachelor of Computer Science (B.sc CS) is a concept-oriented education programme. The bachelor degree imparts nitty- gritties of computer programming, algorithm, computer architecture, etc. Unlike BCA, the curriculum of B.sc CS is not updated, thereby students who are pursuing the course will not get knowledge about current trends and technologies used in coding. Overview of B. Tech Information Technology:

B. Tech Information Technology or B. Tech in IT is an undergraduate engineering programme of four years which prepares students to devise, develop, execute, support and run computer-based information systems.B. Tech Information technology course covers software and hardware aspects. The entire curriculum of B. TechInformation Technology is focused on coding in higher-level languages like C, C++, java, software development and testing, internet technologies, communication and networking, database systems, etc. The course is highly recommended to those students who wish to know the backend aspects of various computer applications and love to play with computers.

Overview of B. Tech Computer Science:

B. Tech IT or B. Tech inCSE Courseis an undergraduate engineering programme of four years, which prepares students to design, implement, and manage information system of software and hardware process. B. Tech Computer Science course lays stress on mathematics, electrical engineering, high-level programming languages, algorithm, data structure, and software architecture.Pursuing the course students go through rigorous theoretical and practical learning, which equips students with cutting-edge technical skills; such as designing software applications, managing network and hardware, writing codes for electrical devices such as printers, scanners, and modems. Besides, the course also covers other aspects such as CAD (computer-assisted design), CAM (computer-assisted manufacturing), world wide web, voice over internet protocol, networking and communications.Nowadays, emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Blockchain Technology has broadened the horizon of B. Tech Computer Science course. Therefore, students who have a keen interest in computer programming and mathematics, and they love to solve complicated technical problems using the concept of mathematical algorithm and coding, they should pursue B. Tech Computer Science.

Comparative Analysis:

B. Tech Computer Science:

B. Tech Computer Science programme mainly lay stress on mathematical aspects of computing. The degreecourse helps students to understand nitty gritties of computer software and hardware and impart skills such as the design of individual microprocessors, personal computers, supercomputers, circuit designing, and writing codes.

B. Tech Information Technology:

B. Tech Information Technology programme mainly focuses onthe management of data and information science and less on mathematical aspects. The degree course prepares students to work effectively with clients, analyze, design, develop and test softwarethat could meet their expectations. Besides, this course also prepares students to use various electronic devices and computer software to store, protect, process, transmit, and retrieve the data securely. Generally, an IT engineer is responsible for maintaining the IT infrastructure of the organization, and he/she performs varieties of tasks including installing applications, design and manage complicated computer networks and information databases.

The Difference in Core Area and Courses:

Major curriculum of B. Tech Computer Science:

Mathematics, Semiconductor Devices and circuits, Network Theory, Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Data Structure, Architecture, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Linear and Digital ICs Applications, Operating Systems, Interfacing through Microprocessors, Theory of Computation, Software Engineering,Robotics, etc.

Major curriculum of B. Tech Information Technology:

The dimension of Information Technology, Basics of Electronics, Engineering Physics and Mathematics, Network Security & Cryptography, Data Mining & Data Warehousing, Artificial Intelligence, Programming Tools & Techniques, Applications of Microprocessor, Management Information Systems, Business Applications of IT, Web Technology, Computer Communication Network, etc.

The Major Difference Between Computer Science and Information Technology:

Simply put, Computer Science is a creation of software and hardware by using programming skills, electrical engineering skills, and mathematical acumen. On the other side, IT is just a selection of proper software and hardware for the task. Allow us to illustrate it by some examples. A laptop, a tablet, a smartphone, search engines like Google, Bing, Yandex, Windows Operating Systems, GPS, social networking sites, PayPal, etc. are examples of IT products and services. All these IT products and services are created by Computer Scientist and installed, tested, run, and maintained by IT professionals as well as Engineers from other disciplines.

Primary Job Responsibilities of Computer Scientists Are:

Developing computer programming languages like Python, Java, Julia, etc.

Development of algorithm.

Development of application software like Android, Cloud Computing, MS word and various mobile applications

Development of operating systems like Windows 10, Linux, Ubuntu, etc.

Programming of computer hardware components.

Development of games and computer software development tools like GitHub, Bracket, Linux, etc.

Primary Job Responsibilities of Information Technology professionals Are:

Development of application software, according to the requirement of clients.

Development of mobile applications like Uber, Ola, Swiggy, and Paytm, etc.

Maintenance of computer software and computer network.

Assuredly, in matter of higher studies and employment opportunities, there are not many differences between these two courses. But, to make a career in IT any specific education is not mandatory, on the other side engineering degree in computer science certainly unlocks the doors ofgreat careers, which otherwise would not be available. Therefore, in the war of Computer Science vs. Information Technology,B. Tech Computer Science programme is betterfor career.

B.Sc. Nursing Vs. GNM Nursing Full Form

The BSc Nursing full form is Bachelor of Science in Nursing, and GNM full form is General Nursing and Midwifery. Undoubtedly, nursing is considered a dignified profession in the world and one of the robust pillars that the medical profession stands on. Nurses play a pivotal role in the healthcare industry; their selfless work and contribution towards sick and infirm people is no less than any doctor. Whether in ward nursing, emergency case handling, or managing the global pandemic, from time to time, nurses have always proven their mettle in all walks of patient care and disease management. Generally, the job responsibility of a Nurse is taking care of infirm people and convalescing them, assisting doctors during examinations and operations, and also handling the administrative responsibilities according to the demands of the situation.

At present, India is facing an acute shortage of nurses. According to the World Health Organisation, in the present scenario patient-to-nurse ratio in the country is 1.7 nurses per 1,000 population, and according to the WHO norm, it should be 3 nurses per 1,000 population, which is 43% less. According to the statistics by the Government of India in March 2020, India has 3.07 million registered nursing personnel, and today the country needs over 24 lakh nurses to overcome the shortage. This acute shortage is prone to a great opportunity in the job market. And due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Indian Government has also realised the importance of a robust healthcare infrastructure in the country. Hence, choosing nursing as a career after 10+2 can be a great option for any student.

After 10+2, there are two popular nursing courses available for students - B.Sc Nursing course andgnm nursing course. Both courses offer good prospects in terms of career and higher education, but it is found that students often remain in a dilemma between these two courses. This post aims to provide clear information about the B.Sc. Nursing course and GNM course that will help you choose a better nursing course after 10+2.

What is GNM Nursing Course

GNM Nursing stands for General Nursing and Midwifery.  It is a diploma course of three and a half years, including an internship of six months. A student who has completed 10+2 in any stream with 45% marks from any recognized board/institute is eligible for the GNM course. The course prepares students to take care of individuals, families, and communities. The GNM course is designed in such a way, it prepares students as nurses and makes them proficient to work in a hospital environment and perform duties like providing first aid, assisting in research activities, wound surgeries and functioning effectively in a team. The course also unlocks the doors of higher education.

BPT admissionis 4½ years undergraduate academic course (including internship of 6 months). AfterBPT admission,during the four years, student studies about the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, exercise therapy, psychology, electrotherapy, research methodology & biostatistics, orthopedics & traumatology, orthopedics and sports physiotherapy, cardio-respiratory & general physiotherapy, neurology & neurosurgery, and neuro-physiotherapy, etc. The objective of the course is to provide a thorough understanding of human anatomy and the intricacies of bones, muscles, and nerves.
